verses.24:2: And he said to the eldest servant of his house, who was over all that he had, "Place your hand under my thigh,
verses.24:3: so that I may make you swear by the Lord God of heaven and earth that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live,
verses.24:4: but will journey to my land and to my relatives, and from there take a wife for my son Isaac."
verses.24:5: The servant answered, "If the woman is not willing to come with me into this land, must I bring your son back to the place from which you came out?"
verses.24:6: Abraham said, "Be careful that you never bring my son back there.
verses.24:7: The Lord God of heaven, who took me from the house of my father and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me and swore, saying, 'I will give this land to your seed,' He Himself will send His angel before you, and from there you will take a wife for my son.
verses.24:8: But if the woman is not willing to follow you, you will not be bound by the oath; only do not bring my son back there."
verses.24:9: Therefore the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore to him about this matter.
verses.24:10: And he took ten camels from his master's herd and departed, carrying with him some of all his goods; and setting out, he proceeded to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
verses.24:11: And when he had made the camels lie down outside the town beside a well of water that evening, at the time when women usually go out to draw water, he said,
verses.24:12: "Lord God of my master Abraham, meet me today, I beg You, and show mercy to my master Abraham.
verses.24:13: Look, I am standing beside the spring of water, and the daughters of the inhabitants of this city will come out to draw water.
verses.24:14: Therefore the young woman to whom I say, 'Lower your jar so that I may drink,' and she answers, 'Drink, and I will even give your camels a drink,' she is the one whom You have prepared for Your servant Isaac; and by this I will understand that You have shown mercy to my master."
verses.24:15: He had not yet finished the words within himself, and look, Rebekah was coming out, the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with a jar on her shoulder,
verses.24:16: a very lovely young woman, and a most beautiful virgin, and unknown to any man. Now she had gone down to the spring, and had filled the jar, and was returning.
verses.24:17: And the servant ran to meet her and said, "Give me a tiny bit of water to sip from your jar."
verses.24:18: She answered, "Drink, my lord." And she quickly lowered the jar onto her forearm and gave him a drink.
verses.24:19: And when he had drunk, she added, "Indeed, I will draw water for your camels as well, until all of them drink."
verses.24:20: And pouring out the jar into the troughs, she ran back to the well to draw water; and when she had drawn it, she gave it to all the camels.
verses.24:21: Now he was gazing at her silently, wanting to know whether the Lord had made his journey prosperous or not.
verses.24:22: Now after the camels had drunk, the man brought out golden earrings weighing two shekels, and just as many bracelets weighing ten shekels.
verses.24:23: And he said to her, "Whose daughter are you? Tell me, is there a place in your father's house to stay?"
verses.24:24: And she replied, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor."
verses.24:25: And she added, saying, "There is also plenty of straw and hay with us, and a spacious place to stay."
verses.24:26: The man bowed down and worshiped the Lord,
verses.24:27: saying, "Blessed be the Lord God of my master Abraham, who has not withdrawn His mercy and truth from my master, and has guided me by a straight path into the house of my master's brother."
verses.24:28: So the young woman ran and reported to her mother's house everything that she had heard.
verses.24:29: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, who went out hurriedly to the man, where the spring was.
verses.24:30: And when he had seen the earrings and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and had heard all the words she reported, "The man spoke these things to me," he came to the man who was standing beside the camels, near the spring of water,
verses.24:31: and said to him, "Enter, blessed of the Lord! Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels."
verses.24:32: And he brought him into the lodging, and unsaddled the camels, and gave straw and hay, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who had come with him.
verses.24:33: And bread was set before him. But he said, "I will not eat until I speak my words." He answered him, "Speak."
verses.24:34: And he said, "I am the servant of Abraham.
verses.24:35: And the Lord has greatly blessed my master, and he has been made great; and He has given him sheep and oxen, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, camels and donkeys.
verses.24:36: And Sarah, the wife of my master, bore a son to my master in her old age, and he gave him all that he possessed.
verses.24:37: And my master made me swear, saying, 'You will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
verses.24:38: but you will go to the house of my father, and from my relatives you will take a wife for my son.'
verses.24:39: But I answered my master, 'What if the woman is not willing to come with me?'
verses.24:40: He said, 'The Lord, in whose sight I walk, will send His angel with you and will direct your way; and you will take a wife for my son from my relatives and from the house of my father.
verses.24:41: You will be innocent of my curse when you come to my kin and they do not give her to you.'
verses.24:42: Therefore I came today to the spring of water and said, 'Lord God of my master Abraham, if You have directed my way on which I now walk,
verses.24:43: look, I am standing beside the spring of water, and the virgin who will come out to draw water hears from me, "Give me a tiny bit of water to drink from your jar,"
verses.24:44: and she says to me, "You drink, and I will draw for your camels as well," she is the woman whom the Lord has prepared for my master's son.'
verses.24:45: While I was silently turning these things over within myself, Rebekah appeared, coming with a jar that she was carrying on her shoulder; and she went down to the spring and drew water. And I said to her, 'Give me a little to drink.'
verses.24:46: And she hurriedly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said to me, 'You drink, and I will give your camels a drink as well.' I drank, and she watered the camels.
verses.24:47: And I asked her and said, 'Whose daughter are you?' She answered, 'I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' Therefore I hung the earrings to adorn her face, and I placed the bracelets on her hands.
verses.24:48: And bowing low, I worshiped the Lord, blessing the Lord God of my master Abraham, who had guided me by a straight path so that I might take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
verses.24:49: For this reason, if you show mercy and truth to my master, tell me; but if something else pleases you, tell me this as well, so that I may go to the right or to the left."
verses.24:50: Laban and Bethuel answered, "The word has come out from the Lord; we cannot speak anything else with you beyond His good pleasure.
verses.24:51: Look, Rebekah is before you: take her and set out, and may she be the wife of the son of your master, just as the Lord has spoken."
verses.24:52: When Abraham's servant had heard this, falling down, he worshiped the Lord to the ground.
verses.24:53: And having brought out vessels of silver and of gold, and garments, he gave them to Rebekah as a gift; he also offered gifts to her brothers and to her mother.
verses.24:54: And when a feast had begun, eating together and drinking, they stayed there. Now rising in the morning, the servant said, "Send me away, so that I may go to my master."
verses.24:55: Her brothers and mother answered, "Let the young woman stay with us at least ten days, and afterward she will set out."
verses.24:56: "Do not detain me," he said, "because the Lord has directed my way; send me away so that I may go to my master."
verses.24:57: They said, "Let us call the young woman and ask her own will."
verses.24:58: And when she had come after being called, they inquired, "Do you want to go with this man?" She said, "I will go."
verses.24:59: Therefore they sent her away, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his companions,
verses.24:60: invoking prosperity upon their sister and saying, "You are our sister; may you grow into a thousand thousands, and may your seed possess the gates of their enemies."
verses.24:61: Therefore Rebekah and her young women, having mounted the camels, followed the man, who was hurriedly returning to his master.
verses.24:62: At that time Isaac was walking along the way that leads to the well whose name is Of the Living and Seeing One, for he lived in the southern land;
verses.24:63: and he had gone out to meditate in the field as the day was already declining; and when he had lifted up his eyes, he saw camels coming in the distance.
verses.24:64: Rebekah also, having caught sight of Isaac, dismounted from the camel,
verses.24:65: and said to the servant, "Who is that man who is coming through the field to meet us?" He said to her, "That is my master." Then she, quickly taking her cloak, covered herself.
verses.24:66: Now the servant recounted to Isaac everything that he had done.
verses.24:67: And he brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother and took her as his wife; and he loved her so greatly that he eased the grief that had arisen from the death of his mother.
verses.25:1: Now Abraham took another wife named Keturah,
verses.25:2: who bore to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
verses.25:3: Jokshan also fathered Sheba and Dedan; the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
verses.25:4: Now from Midian descended Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah; all these were the sons of Keturah.
verses.25:5: And Abraham gave to Isaac all that he had possessed,
verses.25:6: but upon the sons of the concubines he bestowed gifts, and separated them from Isaac his son, while he himself was still living, toward the eastern region.
verses.25:7: Now the days of Abraham's life were one hundred seventy-five years.
verses.25:8: And expiring, he died in a good old age, advanced in years and full of days, and he was gathered to his people.
verses.25:9: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the double cave, which is situated in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, opposite Mamre,
verses.25:10: which he had bought from the sons of Heth; there he himself was buried, and Sarah his wife.
verses.25:11: And after his death, God blessed Isaac his son, who lived near the well by the name of the Living and Seeing One.
verses.25:12: These are the generations of Ishmael the son of Abraham, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to him,
verses.25:13: and these are the names of his sons in their designations and generations. The firstborn of Ishmael was Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
verses.25:15: Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
verses.25:16: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are the names by their villages and towns, twelve princes of their tribes.
verses.25:17: The years of Ishmael's life were one hundred thirty-seven; expiring, he died, and was joined to his people.
verses.25:18: Now he lived from Havilah as far as Shur, which faces Egypt as one enters toward the Assyrians; he died in the presence of all his brothers.
verses.25:19: These also are the generations of Isaac the son of Abraham. Abraham fathered Isaac,
verses.25:20: who, when he was forty years old, took as wife Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian from Mesopotamia, the sister of Laban.
verses.25:21: And Isaac pleaded with the Lord for his wife, because she was barren; and He heard him, and gave conception to Rebekah.
verses.25:22: But the little ones clashed together in her womb, and she said, "If it was going to be this way for me, what need was there to conceive?" And she went to consult the Lord.
verses.25:23: And answering, He said, "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be divided from your belly, and one people will overcome the other people, and the older will serve the younger."
verses.25:24: Now the time for giving birth had come, and look, twins were found in her womb.
verses.25:25: The one who came out first was red, and completely hairy like a pelt; and his name was called Esau. Immediately the other, coming out, was holding the sole of his brother's foot with his hand, and for that reason she named him Jacob.
verses.25:26: Isaac was sixty years old when the little ones were born to him.
verses.25:27: When they had grown up, Esau became a man skilled in hunting and a farmer, while Jacob, a simple man, lived in tents.
verses.25:28: Isaac loved Esau, because he ate of his game; and Rebekah loved Jacob.
verses.25:29: Now Jacob cooked a stew; and when Esau had come to him from the field weary,
verses.25:30: he said, "Give me some of this red cooked dish, because I am exceedingly weary." For this reason his name was called Edom.
verses.25:31: To him Jacob said, "Sell me your birthright."
verses.25:32: He answered, "Look, I am dying; what benefit will the birthright be to me?"
verses.25:33: Jacob said, "Swear to me, then." Esau swore to him and sold the birthright.
verses.25:34: And so, having received bread and a dish of lentils, he ate and drank, and went away, regarding it as a small thing that he had sold the birthright.
verses.26:1: Now when a famine arose over the land after that barrenness which had happened in the days of Abraham, Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, in Gerar.
verses.26:2: And the Lord appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt, but rest in the land of which I will tell you,
verses.26:3: and live as a foreigner in it; and I will be with you and will bless you, for to you and to your seed I will give all these regions, fulfilling the oath that I pledged to Abraham your father.
verses.26:4: And I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your descendants all these regions; and in your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed,
verses.26:5: because Abraham obeyed My voice, and kept My precepts and My commandments, and observed the ceremonies and laws."
verses.26:7: When he was questioned by the men of that place about his wife, he answered, "She is my sister." For he had been afraid to admit that she was joined to him in marriage, thinking that they might perhaps kill him on account of her beauty.
verses.26:8: And when very many days had passed and he was staying there, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looking out through a window, saw him playing with Rebekah his wife.
verses.26:9: And summoning him, he said, "It is clear that she is your wife; why did you lie that she was your sister?" He answered, "I was afraid that I might die because of her."
verses.26:10: And Abimelech said, "Why have you deceived us? Someone from the people could have lain with your wife, and you would have brought a great sin upon us." And he commanded all the people, saying,
verses.26:11: "Whoever touches this man's wife will certainly die."
verses.26:12: Now Isaac sowed in that land, and found a hundredfold in that same year; and the Lord blessed him.
verses.26:13: And the man became rich, and he kept going forward and growing until he became exceedingly great;
verses.26:14: he also had possessions of sheep and herds, and a very large household. Because of this, the Philistines, envying him,
verses.26:15: at that time stopped up all the wells that the servants of his father Abraham had dug, filling them with earth,
verses.26:16: to such an extent that Abimelech himself said to Isaac, "Depart from us, because you have become far more powerful than we."
verses.26:17: And departing so that he might come to the torrent-bed of Gerar and live there,
verses.26:18: he dug again other wells, which the servants of his father Abraham had dug, and which, after his death, the Philistines had formerly stopped up; and he named them with the same names by which his father had called them before.
verses.26:19: They dug in the torrent-bed and found living water.
verses.26:20: But there also the shepherds of Gerar had a quarrel against the shepherds of Isaac, saying, "The water is ours." For this reason, from what had happened, he called the name of the well False Claim.
verses.26:21: They dug another one also, and over that one too they disputed, and he named it Hostility.
verses.26:22: Setting out from there, he dug another well, over which they did not contend; therefore he called its name Spaciousness, saying, "Now the Lord has made room for us and caused us to grow over the land."
verses.26:23: Now he went up from that place to Beersheba,
verses.26:24: where the Lord appeared to him on that very night, saying, "I am the God of Abraham your father; do not be afraid, because I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your seed for the sake of My servant Abraham."
verses.26:25: So he built an altar there, and having called upon the name of the Lord, he pitched a tent, and commanded his servants to dig a well.
verses.26:26: When Abimelech, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol, commander of the soldiers, had come to that place from Gerar,
verses.26:27: Isaac spoke to them, "Why have you come to me, a man whom you hate and have driven away from you?"
verses.26:28: They answered, "We have seen that the Lord is with you, and for that reason we ourselves have said, 'Let there be an oath between us, and let us enter into a covenant,
verses.26:29: that you will not do us any evil, just as we also have touched nothing of yours, nor have we done anything that would harm you, but we sent you away in peace, enriched by the blessing of the Lord.'"
verses.26:30: So he made a feast for them, and after food and drink,
verses.26:31: rising in the morning, they swore to one another; and Isaac sent them away peacefully to their own place.
verses.26:32: Now look, on that very day the servants of Isaac came, reporting to him about the well that they had dug, and saying, "We have found water."
verses.26:33: Because of this he named it Abundance, and the name Beersheba was given to the city, down to the present day.
verses.26:34: Now Esau, when he was forty years old, took as wives Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon of the same place,
verses.26:35: both of whom had offended the spirit of Isaac and Rebekah.
verses.27:1: Now Isaac grew old, and his eyes grew dim, and he could not see. And he called Esau, his older son, and said to him, "My son?" And he answered, "Here I am."
verses.27:2: His father said to him, "You see that I have grown old, and I do not know the day of my death.
verses.27:3: Take your weapons, quiver and bow, and go outside; and when you have caught something by hunting,
verses.27:4: make me a savory dish from it, just as you know I desire, and bring it so that I may eat, and my soul may bless you before I die."
verses.27:5: When Rebekah had heard this, and he had gone off into the field to fulfill his father's command,
verses.27:6: she said to her son Jacob, "I heard your father speaking with your brother Esau and saying to him,
verses.27:7: 'Bring me some of your game and make food so that I may eat and bless you before the Lord before I die.'
verses.27:8: Now therefore, my son, yield to my counsel:
verses.27:9: and going to the flock, bring me two of the finest young goats, so that I may make dishes from them for your father, which he gladly eats,
verses.27:10: and when you have brought them in and he has eaten, he may bless you before he dies."
verses.27:11: He answered her, "You know that my brother Esau is a hairy man, and I am smooth;
verses.27:12: if my father touches me and notices, I am afraid that he will think I wanted to mock him, and I will bring a curse upon myself instead of a blessing."
verses.27:13: To him his mother said, "Let that curse be upon me, my son; only listen to my voice, and go and bring what I said."
verses.27:14: He went off and brought them, and gave them to his mother. She prepared the food, just as she knew his father desired.
verses.27:15: And she dressed him in the very fine garments of Esau, which she had with her at home,
verses.27:16: and she wrapped the skins of the young goats around his hands, and covered the bare parts of his neck;
verses.27:17: she gave him the savory dish, and handed over the loaves of bread that she had baked.
verses.27:18: After bringing them in, he said, "My father?" And he answered, "I am listening. Who are you, my son?"
verses.27:19: And Jacob said, "I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done just as you commanded me: rise, sit up, and eat from my game, so that your soul may bless me."
verses.27:20: Again Isaac said to his son, "How were you able to find it so quickly, my son?" And he answered, "It was the will of God that what I wanted should quickly come before me."
verses.27:21: And Isaac said, "Come closer here, so that I may touch you, my son, and test whether you are my son Esau or not."
verses.27:22: He approached his father, and after feeling him, Isaac said, "The voice is indeed Jacob's voice, yet the hands are Esau's hands."
verses.27:23: And he did not recognize him, because the hairy hands had reproduced the likeness of the older son. Blessing him, therefore,
verses.27:24: he said, "Are you my son Esau?" He answered, "I am."
verses.27:25: And he said, "Bring me food from your game, my son, so that my soul may bless you." When it was brought and he had eaten it, he also brought him wine. After drinking it,
verses.27:26: he said to him, "Come close to me, and give me a kiss, my son."
verses.27:27: He approached and kissed him. And as soon as he smelled the fragrance of his garments, blessing him, he said, "See, the scent of my son is like the scent of a full field that the Lord has blessed.
verses.27:28: May God give you from the dew of heaven and from the richness of the earth an abundance of grain and wine.
verses.27:29: And may peoples serve you, and may tribes pay homage to you; be lord over your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down before you. Whoever curses you, let him be cursed, and whoever blesses you, let him be filled with blessings."
verses.27:30: Isaac had scarcely finished his speech, and when Jacob had gone outside, Esau came,
verses.27:31: and brought in to his father food cooked from his game, saying, "Rise, my father, and eat from your son's game, so that your soul may bless me."
verses.27:32: And Isaac said to him, "Who then are you?" And he answered, "I am your firstborn son, Esau."
verses.27:33: Isaac trembled with violent astonishment, and marveling beyond what can be believed, he said, "Who then is he who just now brought me caught game, and I ate from everything before you came, and I blessed him, and he will be blessed?"
verses.27:34: When Esau heard his father's words, he roared out with a great cry, and distraught, he said, "Bless me also, my father."
verses.27:35: And he said, "Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing."
verses.27:36: And he added, "Rightly has his name been called Jacob, for look, he has supplanted me a second time: previously he took away my birthright, and now a second time he has stolen my blessing." And again to his father he said, "Have you not reserved a blessing for me too?"
verses.27:37: Isaac answered, "I have appointed him as your lord, and all his brothers I have subjected to his service; with grain and wine I have established him. After these things, my son, what further can I do for you?"
verses.27:38: To him Esau said, "Do you have only one blessing, father? I beg you to bless me as well." And as he wept with a loud wailing,
verses.27:39: being moved, Isaac said to him, "In the richness of the earth and in the dew of heaven from above,
verses.27:40: your blessing will be. You will live by the sword, and you will serve your brother; and a time will come when you will shake off and loosen his yoke from your neck."
verses.27:41: Therefore Esau always hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him; and he said in his heart, "The days of mourning for my father will come, and I will kill my brother Jacob."
verses.27:42: These things were reported to Rebekah; and sending and calling her son Jacob, she said to him, "Look, your brother Esau is threatening to kill you.
verses.27:43: Now therefore, my son, listen to my voice, and rising up, flee to my brother Laban in Haran;
verses.27:44: and you will dwell with him a few days, until your brother's fury subsides,
verses.27:45: and his indignation ceases, and he forgets the things that you did against him. Afterward I will send and bring you from there to here. Why should I be bereaved of both sons in one day?"
verses.27:46: Rebekah also said to Isaac, "I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth; if Jacob takes a wife from the stock of this land, I do not want to live."
verses.28:1: Therefore Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him and commanded him, saying, "Do not take a wife from the lineage of Canaan;
verses.28:2: but go and set out for Mesopotamia of Syria, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take for yourself a wife from there, from the daughters of Laban, your uncle.
verses.28:3: And may Almighty God bless you, and make you grow and multiply you, so that you may become multitudes of peoples.
verses.28:4: And may He give the blessings of Abraham to you and to your seed after you, so that you may possess the land of your sojourning, which He promised to your grandfather."
verses.28:5: And when Isaac had sent him away, he set out and came to Mesopotamia of Syria, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of his mother Rebekah.
verses.28:6: Now Esau, seeing that his father had blessed Jacob and had sent him to Mesopotamia of Syria to take a wife from there, and that after the blessing he had commanded him, saying, "You will not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,"
verses.28:7: and that Jacob, obeying his parents, had gone to Syria,
verses.28:8: realizing also that his father did not look gladly upon the daughters of Canaan,
verses.28:9: went to Ishmael, and took as a wife, besides those whom he previously had, Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, son of Abraham, the sister of Nebaioth.
verses.28:10: Therefore Jacob, departing from Beersheba, was journeying toward Haran.
verses.28:11: And when he had come to a certain place, and wanted to rest in it after the setting of the sun, he took from the stones that were lying there, and placing one under his head, he slept in that same place.
verses.28:12: And he saw in a dream a ladder standing on the earth, with its summit touching heaven, and angels of God also ascending and descending along it,
verses.28:13: and the Lord leaning upon the ladder, saying to him, "I am the Lord God of your father Abraham, and the God of Isaac. The land on which you sleep, I will give to you and to your seed.
verses.28:14: And your seed will be like the dust of the earth; you will spread out to the west and the east, the north and the south; and in you and in your seed all the tribes of the earth will be blessed.
verses.28:15: And I will be your guardian wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land; nor will I leave you unless I have fulfilled everything that I have spoken."
verses.28:16: And when Jacob awoke from sleep, he said, "Truly the Lord is in this place, and I did not know."
verses.28:17: And trembling with fear, he said, "How fearful is this place! There is nothing else here except the house of God, and the gate of heaven."
verses.28:18: Rising in the morning, therefore, Jacob took the stone that he had placed under his head, and set it up as a monument, pouring oil on top of it.
verses.28:19: And he called the name of the city Bethel, which was previously called Luz.
verses.28:20: He also vowed a vow, saying, "If God is with me, and guards me on the way along which I walk, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to put on,
verses.28:21: and I return prosperously to my father's house, the Lord will be God to me,
verses.28:22: and this stone, which I have set up as a monument, will be called the House of God; and of all things that You give me, I will offer tithes to You."
verses.29:1: So Jacob set out and came to the eastern land.
verses.29:2: And he saw a well in a field, and three flocks of sheep lying down beside it; for from it the livestock were watered, and its mouth was closed with a large stone.
verses.29:3: And it was the custom that when all the sheep were gathered together, they would roll away the stone, and when the flocks were refreshed, they would place it back over the mouth of the well.
verses.29:4: And he said to the shepherds, "Brothers, where are you from?" And they answered, "From Haran."
verses.29:5: Questioning them, he said, "Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?" They said, "We know him."
verses.29:6: "Is he well?" he said. "He is well," they said, "and look, his daughter Rachel is coming with her flock."
verses.29:7: And Jacob said, "Much of the day is still left, and it is not time for the flocks to be brought back to the sheepfolds; give drink to the sheep first, and then bring them back to pasture."
verses.29:8: And they answered, "We cannot until all the livestock are gathered together and we move the stone away from the mouth of the well, so that we may water the flocks."
verses.29:9: They were still speaking, and look, Rachel was coming with her father's sheep, for she herself was tending the flock.
verses.29:10: And when Jacob saw her and knew that she was his cousin, and that the sheep were those of Laban, his uncle, he moved away the stone with which the well was closed.
verses.29:11: And when the flock had been watered, he kissed her, and raising his voice, he wept,
verses.29:12: and told her that he was her father's brother and the son of Rebekah; and she hurried and reported it to her father.
verses.29:13: And when he heard that Jacob, his sister's son, had come, he ran to meet him, and embracing him and falling on him with kisses, he led him into his house. And having heard the reasons for the journey,
verses.29:14: he answered, "You are my bone and my flesh." And after the days of one month were completed,
verses.29:15: he said to him, "Because you are my brother, will you serve me for nothing? Tell me what wages you should receive."
verses.29:16: Now he had two daughters: the name of the older one was Leah, and the younger one was called Rachel.
verses.29:17: But Leah had bleary eyes; Rachel was beautiful in face and lovely in appearance.
verses.29:18: Loving her, Jacob said, "I will serve you for Rachel, your younger daughter, for seven years."
verses.29:19: Laban replied, "It is better for me to give her to you than to another man; remain with me."
verses.29:20: Therefore Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him a few days because of the magnitude of his love.
verses.29:21: And he said to Laban, "Give me my wife, because the time is already completed, so that I may go in to her."
verses.29:22: And having called many crowds of friends to a banquet, he held the wedding.
verses.29:23: And in the evening he led his daughter Leah in to him,
verses.29:24: giving his daughter a maidservant, Zilpah by name. And when Jacob had gone in to her as was customary, once morning arrived he saw Leah,
verses.29:25: and he said to his father-in-law, "What is it that you wanted to do? Did I not serve you for Rachel? Why did you deceive me?"
verses.29:26: Laban answered, "It is not the custom in our place for us to give the younger ones in marriage first.
verses.29:27: Complete the week of days of this union, and I will give you this one also for the work by which you will serve me for another seven years."
verses.29:28: He agreed to the terms, and when the week had passed, he took Rachel as his wife,
verses.29:29: to whom her father had given the servant Bilhah.
verses.29:30: And at last, having obtained the longed-for marriage, he placed his love for the second one ahead of the first, serving with him for another seven years.
verses.29:31: Now when the Lord saw that he despised Leah, He opened her womb, while her sister remained barren.
verses.29:32: And she conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben, saying, "The Lord has seen my humiliation; now my husband will love me."
verses.29:33: And again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, "Because the Lord has heard that I am held in contempt, He has given this one also to me." And she called his name Simeon.
verses.29:34: And she conceived a third time and bore another son, and said, "Now too my husband will be united to me, because I have given birth to three sons for him." And for that reason she gave him the name Levi.
verses.29:35: A fourth time she conceived and gave birth to a son, and said, "Now I will give praise to the Lord." And because of this she called him Judah, and she stopped giving birth.
verses.30:1: Now Rachel, seeing that she was barren, envied her sister and said to her husband, "Give me children, otherwise I will die."
verses.30:2: Jacob, angry with her, answered, "Am I in the place of God, who has deprived you of the fruit of your womb?"
verses.30:3: But she said, "I have a maidservant, Bilhah; go in to her, so that she may give birth upon my knees, and I may have sons from her."
verses.30:4: And she gave Bilhah to him in marriage; and she,
verses.30:5: after her husband had gone in to her, conceived and bore a son.
verses.30:6: And Rachel said, "The Lord has judged for me and has heard my voice, giving me a son," and therefore she called his name Dan.
verses.30:7: And Bilhah, conceiving again, bore another,
verses.30:8: on whose account Rachel said, "God has matched me with my sister, and I have prevailed." And she called him Naphtali.
verses.30:9: Leah, realizing that she had stopped giving birth, handed over her maidservant Zilpah to her husband.
verses.30:10: When she brought forth a son after conception,
verses.30:11: she said, "Fortunately!" and therefore she called his name Gad.
verses.30:13: And Leah said, "This is for my blessedness, for indeed women will call me blessed." For this reason she called him Asher.
verses.30:14: Now Reuben went out into the field at the time of the wheat harvest and found mandrakes, which he brought to his mother Leah. And Rachel said, "Give me a portion of your son's mandrakes."
verses.30:15: She answered, "Does it seem too little to you that you have taken my husband away from me, unless you also take my son's mandrakes?" Rachel said, "Let him sleep with you tonight for your son's mandrakes."
verses.30:16: And as Jacob was returning from the field toward evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, "You will come in to me, because I have hired you for wages in exchange for my son's mandrakes." And he slept with her that night.
verses.30:17: And God heard her prayers, and she conceived and bore a fifth son,
verses.30:18: and said, "God has given me wages, because I gave my maidservant to my husband." And she called his name Issachar.
verses.30:19: Leah, conceiving again, bore a sixth son,
verses.30:20: and said, "God has endowed me with a good dowry; this time also my husband will be with me, because I have borne him six sons." And therefore she called his name Zebulun.
verses.30:21: After him she bore a daughter, named Dinah.
verses.30:22: The Lord also remembered Rachel, heard her, and opened her womb.
verses.30:23: And she conceived and bore a son, saying, "God has removed my disgrace."
verses.30:24: And she called his name Joseph, saying, "May the Lord add another son to me."
verses.30:25: Now when Joseph had been born, Jacob said to his father-in-law, "Let me go, so that I may return to my homeland and to my land.
verses.30:26: Give me my wives and children, for whom I have served you, so that I may depart; you know the service with which I have served you."
verses.30:27: Laban said to him, "May I find favor in your sight; I have learned by experience that God has blessed me on account of you;
verses.30:28: set your wages for me to give to you."
verses.30:29: But he answered, "You know how I have served you, and how great your property has been in my hands.
verses.30:30: You had little before I came to you, and now you have become rich; and the Lord has blessed you at my entrance. It is right, therefore, that at last I should also provide for my own household."
verses.30:31: And Laban said, "What shall I give you?" But he said, "I want nothing; but if you do what I ask, I will again pasture and guard your livestock.
verses.30:32: Go around all your flocks and separate all the sheep that are variegated and of flecked fleece; and whatever is dark, and spotted, and variegated, both among the sheep and among the goats, will be my wages.
verses.30:33: And my righteousness will answer for me tomorrow, when the time of the agreement comes before you; and all that are not variegated, and spotted, and dark, both among the sheep and among the goats, will convict me of theft."
verses.30:34: Laban said, "I am pleased with what you ask."
verses.30:35: And on that day he separated the female goats and ewes, the male goats and rams that were variegated and spotted; but the entire single-colored flock, that is, of white and black fleece, he delivered into the hand of his sons.
verses.30:36: And he set a distance of a three days' journey between himself and his son-in-law, who was pasturing his remaining flocks.
verses.30:37: Jacob, therefore, took green rods of poplar, of almond, and from plane trees, and partly peeled them; and when the bark had been stripped off, in the places that had been bared, whiteness appeared, while those that were intact remained green; and in this manner the color became variegated.
verses.30:38: And he placed them in the troughs where the water was poured out, so that when the flocks came to drink, they would have the rods before their eyes and would conceive at the sight of them.
verses.30:39: And it happened that in the very heat of mating, the sheep gazed upon the rods and bore young that were spotted, and variegated, and speckled with diverse color.
verses.30:40: And Jacob divided the flock and placed the rods in the troughs before the eyes of the rams; now all the white and the black ones belonged to Laban, while the rest belonged to Jacob, with the flocks separated from one another.
verses.30:41: Therefore, whenever the ewes were mounted at the first season, Jacob would place the rods in the water troughs before the eyes of the rams and ewes, so that they would conceive while gazing at them;
verses.30:42: but when it was the late mating and the final conception, he would not place them. And those that were of the late season became Laban's, and those of the first season, Jacob's.
verses.30:43: And the man was enriched beyond measure, and he had many flocks, female servants and male servants, camels and donkeys.
verses.31:1: Now after he heard the words of Laban's sons saying, "Jacob has taken all that belonged to our father, and having grown rich from his property, he has become renowned,"
verses.31:2: he also noticed Laban's face, that it was not toward him as yesterday and the day before yesterday,
verses.31:3: especially with the Lord saying to him, "Return to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I will be with you."
verses.31:4: He sent and called Rachel and Leah into the field where he was pasturing the flocks,
verses.31:5: and said to them, "I see your father's face, that it is not toward me as yesterday and the day before yesterday; but the God of my father has been with me.
verses.31:6: And you yourselves know that I have served your father with all my strength.
verses.31:7: But your father deceived me and changed my wages ten times; and yet God did not allow him to harm me.
verses.31:8: Whenever he said, 'Your wages will be speckled,' all the sheep bore speckled young; but when, on the contrary, he said, 'All the white ones you will receive as wages,' all the flocks bore white ones.
verses.31:9: And God took away your father's possessions and gave them to me.
verses.31:10: For after the time of the sheep's conception had arrived, I lifted up my eyes and saw in a dream the males mounting the females, speckled and spotted and of different colors.
verses.31:11: And the angel of God said to me in a dream, 'Jacob?' And I answered, 'Here I am.'
verses.31:12: He said, 'Lift up your eyes and see all the males mounting the females, speckled, flecked, and spotted. For I have seen all that Laban has done to you.
verses.31:13: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the stone and vowed a vow to Me. Now therefore, rise and go out from this land, returning to the land of your birth.'"
verses.31:14: Rachel and Leah answered, "Do we have anything remaining in the property and inheritance of our father's house?
verses.31:15: Has he not regarded us as foreigners, and sold us, and consumed our price?
verses.31:16: But God has taken away our father's wealth and handed it over to us and to our children; therefore do all that God has commanded you."
verses.31:17: So Jacob rose up, and having placed his children and his wives on camels, departed.
verses.31:18: And he took all his possessions and flocks, and whatever he had acquired in Mesopotamia, going to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.
verses.31:19: At that time Laban had gone to shear the sheep, and Rachel stole her father's idols.
verses.31:20: And Jacob was unwilling to disclose to his father-in-law that he was fleeing.
verses.31:21: And when both he himself and all that belonged to him had departed, and after crossing the river he was heading toward Mount Gilead,
verses.31:22: it was reported to Laban on the third day that Jacob was fleeing.
verses.31:23: Taking his brothers with him, he pursued him for seven days and overtook him on Mount Gilead.
verses.31:24: And in a dream he saw God saying to him, "Be careful not to speak anything harshly against Jacob."
verses.31:25: Now Jacob had already pitched his tent on the mountain, when he caught up with him along with his brothers and set up his tent on the same Mount Gilead.
verses.31:26: And he said to Jacob, "Why have you acted like this, that without my knowledge you drove away my daughters like captives of the sword?
verses.31:27: Why did you want to flee while I was unaware, and not inform me, so that I might send you off with joy, and songs, and tambourines, and lyres?
verses.31:28: You did not allow me to kiss my sons and daughters; you have acted foolishly; and now
verses.31:29: my hand indeed has the power to repay you with harm; but the God of your father said to me yesterday, 'Be careful not to speak anything too harsh against Jacob.'
verses.31:30: Granted, you desired to go to your own people, and you had a longing for your father's house; why did you steal my gods?"
verses.31:31: Jacob answered, "As for setting out without your knowledge, I was afraid that you would take away your daughters by force.
verses.31:32: But as for your accusing me of theft, with whomever you find your gods, let him be put to death before our brothers; search out whatever of yours you find with me, and take it away." Saying these things, he did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.
verses.31:33: So Laban entered the tent of Jacob, and of Leah, and of both maidservants; he did not find them. And when he had entered Rachel's tent,
verses.31:34: hurrying, she hid the idols under the camel's bedding and sat on top; and as he searched the whole tent and found nothing,
verses.31:35: she said, "Let my lord not be angry that I cannot rise before you, for it has now happened to me according to the custom of women." Thus the diligence of the one searching was foiled.
verses.31:36: And Jacob, swelling with anger, said in contention, "For what fault of mine, and for what sin of mine, have you burned so hotly after me,
verses.31:37: and searched all my household goods? What have you found of all the possessions of your house? Set it here before my brothers and your brothers, and let them judge between me and you.
verses.31:38: Was it for this that I have been with you twenty years? Your sheep and goats were not barren; the rams of your flock I did not eat;
verses.31:39: nor did I show you what was seized by a beast; I myself repaid every loss; whatever was lost by theft, you demanded from me;
verses.31:40: day and night I was burned by heat and by frost; sleep fled from my eyes.
verses.31:41: Thus for twenty years in your house I served you, fourteen for your daughters and six for your flocks; you also changed my wages ten times.
verses.31:42: Unless the God of my father Abraham and the fear of Isaac had been with me, perhaps now you would have sent me away naked; God has looked upon my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you yesterday."
verses.31:43: Laban answered him, "My daughters and the children, and your flocks, and all that you see, are mine; what can I do to my children and my grandchildren?
verses.31:44: Come therefore, and let us enter into a covenant, so that it may be a testimony between me and you."
verses.31:45: So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a monument,
verses.31:46: and said to his brothers, "Bring stones." Gathering them, they made a mound and ate on it;
verses.31:47: which Laban called Mound of Witness, and Jacob, Heap of Testimony, each according to the idiom of his own language.
verses.31:48: And Laban said, "This mound will be a witness between me and you today," and for this reason its name was called Gilead, that is, Mound of Witness.
verses.31:49: "May the Lord watch and judge between us when we have departed from one another,
verses.31:50: if you afflict my daughters, and if you bring in other wives besides them; there is no witness to our word except God, who is present and looks on."
verses.31:51: And he said again to Jacob, "Look, this mound and the stone which I have set up between me and you,
verses.31:52: will be a witness: let this mound, I say, and the stone be for a testimony, if either I pass beyond it going to you, or you pass by, devising harm against me.
verses.31:53: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor judge between us, the God of their father." Jacob swore by the fear of his father Isaac,
verses.31:54: and having offered sacrifices on the mountain, he called his brothers to eat bread. And when they had eaten, they remained there.
verses.31:55: Now Laban, rising up in the night, kissed his sons and his daughters and blessed them, returning to his own place.
verses.32:1: Jacob also went on along the journey he had begun, and angels of God met him.
verses.32:2: When he saw them, he said, "This is the camp of God," and he called the name of that place Mahanaim, that is, Camp.
verses.32:3: He also sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, in the region of Edom,
verses.32:4: and he commanded them, saying, "Speak in this way to my lord Esau: 'This is what your brother Jacob says: I have lived as a foreigner with Laban and have remained until the present day.
verses.32:5: I have cattle and donkeys, sheep, and male servants and female servants, and now I am sending a delegation to my lord so that I may find favor in your sight.'"
verses.32:6: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, "We came to your brother Esau, and look, he is hurrying to meet you with four hundred men."
verses.32:7: Jacob was greatly afraid, and, terrified, he divided the people who were with him, as well as the herds, and the sheep, and the cattle, and the camels, into two companies,
verses.32:8: saying, "If Esau comes to one company and strikes it, the other company that remains will be saved."
verses.32:9: And Jacob said, "God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, Lord who said to me, 'Return to your land and to the place of your birth, and I will do good to you,'
verses.32:10: I am less than all Your mercies and Your truth that You have fulfilled for Your servant. With my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I am returning with two companies.
verses.32:11: Rescue me from the hand of my brother Esau, because I am greatly afraid of him, so that he might not come and strike the mother with the children.
verses.32:12: You said that You would do good to me and would expand my seed like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted because of its multitude."
verses.32:13: And when he had slept there that night, he set apart from the things that he had gifts for his brother Esau:
verses.32:14: two hundred female goats, twenty male goats, two hundred ewes, twenty rams,
verses.32:15: thirty nursing female camels with their young, forty cows and twenty bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten of their young.
verses.32:16: And he sent each herd separately by the hands of his servants, and he said to his attendants, "Go ahead of me, and let there be a space between herd and herd."
verses.32:17: And he commanded the first, saying, "If you meet my brother Esau and he asks you, 'Whose are you?' or, 'Where are you going?' or, 'Whose are these that you are following?'
verses.32:18: you will answer, 'Your servant Jacob's; he has sent gifts to my lord Esau, and he himself is also coming behind us.'"
verses.32:19: In the same way he gave orders to the second and the third, and to all who were following the herds, saying, "Speak with the same words to Esau when you find him.
verses.32:20: And you will add, 'Your servant Jacob himself is also following our path.'" For he said, "I will appease him with the gifts that go ahead, and afterward I will see him; perhaps he will be favorable to me."
verses.32:21: So the gifts went on ahead of him, but he himself stayed that night in the camp.
verses.32:22: And when he had risen early, he took his two wives and the same number of female servants, with eleven sons, and crossed the ford of Jabbok.
verses.32:23: And after everything that belonged to him had been brought across,
verses.32:24: he remained alone; and look, a man was wrestling with him until morning.
verses.32:25: When he saw that he could not overpower him, he touched the sinew of his thigh, and immediately it withered.
verses.32:26: And he said to him, "Let me go, for dawn is already rising." He answered, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
verses.32:27: So he said, "What is your name?" He answered, "Jacob."
verses.32:28: But he said, "By no means will your name be called Jacob, but Israel; for if you have been strong against God, how much more will you prevail against men?"
verses.32:29: Jacob asked him, "Tell me, by what name are you called?" He answered, "Why do you ask my name?" And he blessed him in that same place.
verses.32:30: And Jacob called the name of that place Penuel, saying, "I have seen God face to face, and my life has been saved."
verses.32:31: And immediately the sun rose upon him after he passed beyond Penuel, but he himself was limping on his foot.
verses.32:32: For this reason the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew that withered in Jacob's thigh until the present day, because he touched the sinew of his thigh and it grew numb.
verses.33:1: Now Jacob, lifting up his eyes, saw Esau coming, and with him four hundred men; and he divided the children of Leah and Rachel, and of both female servants,
verses.33:2: and he placed both maidservants and their children at the front, Leah and her children in the second place, and Rachel and Joseph last.
verses.33:3: And he himself, going ahead, bowed down prostrate to the ground seven times until his brother approached.
verses.33:4: So Esau, running to meet his brother, embraced him, and clasping his neck and kissing him, he wept.
verses.33:5: And lifting up his eyes, he saw the women and their little ones, and said, "What do these mean, and do they belong to you?" He answered, "They are the little ones whom God has granted to me, your servant."
verses.33:6: And the maidservants and their children approached and bowed low.
verses.33:7: And Leah came forward with her children, and when they had bowed down in the same way, last of all Joseph and Rachel bowed down.
verses.33:8: Esau said, "What are these companies that I met?" He answered, "So that I might find favor before my lord."
verses.33:9: And he said, "I have very much, my brother; let what is yours be yours."
verses.33:10: Jacob said, "Do not do so, I beg you, but if I have found favor in your eyes, accept a small gift from my hands. For I have seen your face as though I had seen the countenance of God; be favorable to me,
verses.33:11: and receive the blessing that I have brought to you and that God has granted to me, bestowing all things." Receiving it only with difficulty as his brother urged him,
verses.33:12: he said, "Let us walk together, and I will be a companion of your journey."
verses.33:13: Jacob said, "You know, my lord, that I have tender little ones and nursing sheep and cattle with me; if I make them labor too much in walking, all the herds will die in one day.
verses.33:14: Let my lord go ahead before his servant, and I will follow his footsteps little by little, as I see that my little ones are able, until I come to my lord in Seir."
verses.33:15: Esau answered, "I ask you that, from the people who are with me, companions at least may remain for your way." He said, "It is not necessary; I need this one thing only, that I may find favor in your sight, my lord."
verses.33:16: So Esau returned on that day to Seir by the way he had come.
verses.33:17: And Jacob came to Succoth, where, after building a house and pitching tents, he called the name of that place Succoth, that is, Tabernacles.
verses.33:18: And he crossed over to Salem, the city of the Shechemites, which is in the land of Canaan, after he returned from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he lived beside the town.
verses.33:19: And he bought the portion of the field in which he had pitched his tents from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred lambs.
verses.33:20: And after erecting an altar there, he called upon the most mighty God of Israel over it.
verses.34:1: Now Dinah, the daughter of Leah, went out to see the women of that region.
verses.34:2: When Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of that land, saw her, he fell in love with her and seized her, and he slept with her, overpowering the virgin by force.
verses.34:3: And his soul was closely bound to her, and in her sorrow he soothed her with gentle words.
verses.34:4: And going to his father Hamor, he said, "Take this girl for me as a wife."
verses.34:5: When Jacob heard this, while his sons were absent and occupied in pasturing the livestock, he kept silent until they returned.
verses.34:6: Now when Hamor, the father of Shechem, had gone out to speak to Jacob,
verses.34:7: look, his sons were coming from the field; and when they heard what had happened, they were very angry, because he had done a disgraceful thing in Israel and, having violated the daughter of Jacob, had committed an unlawful deed.
verses.34:8: So Hamor spoke to them: "The soul of my son Shechem has clung to your daughter; give her to him as a wife,
verses.34:9: and let us join in marriage with one another; give your daughters to us, and take our daughters,
verses.34:10: and live with us; the land is in your power: cultivate it, trade, and possess it."
verses.34:11: Shechem also said to her father and to her brothers, "Let me find favor before you, and whatever you determine, I will give;
verses.34:12: increase the dowry, demand gifts; I will gladly grant what you ask; only give me this girl as a wife."
verses.34:13: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and his father with deceit, raging because of the defilement of their sister:
verses.34:14: "We cannot do what you ask, nor give our sister to an uncircumcised man, which is unlawful and abominable among us.
verses.34:15: But on this condition we will be able to enter into an alliance: if you are willing to be like us, and everyone of the male sex among you is circumcised;
verses.34:16: then we will mutually give and take your daughters and ours, and we will live with you, and we will be one people.
verses.34:17: But if you are unwilling to be circumcised, we will take our daughter and depart."
verses.34:18: Their proposal pleased Hamor and his son Shechem,
verses.34:19: and the young man did not delay in immediately fulfilling what was asked, for he loved the girl very much, and he himself was renowned in all the house of his father.
verses.34:20: And having entered the gate of the city, they spoke to the people:
verses.34:21: "These men are peaceful and wish to live with us; let them trade in the land and cultivate it, for being spacious and wide it needs cultivators; we will take their daughters as wives, and we will give ours to them.
verses.34:22: There is one thing by which so great a good is delayed: if we circumcise our males, imitating the rite of the nation.
verses.34:23: And their property, and their livestock, and all that they possess will be ours; only let us consent to this, and living together, we will form one people."
verses.34:24: All agreed, and all the males were circumcised.
verses.34:25: And look, on the third day, when the pain of the wounds is most severe, two sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dinah, having seized their swords, entered the city boldly; and having killed all the males,
verses.34:26: they put Hamor and Shechem to death together, taking Dinah their sister from the house of Shechem.
verses.34:27: When they had gone out, the rest of the sons of Jacob rushed upon those who had been killed and pillaged the city in vengeance for the defilement.
verses.34:28: Plundering their sheep, and herds, and donkeys, and everything that was in the houses and in the fields,
verses.34:29: they also led away their little ones and their wives captive.
verses.34:30: When these things had been audaciously carried out, Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have troubled me and made me hateful to the Canaanites and the Perizzites, the inhabitants of this land; we are few; they will gather together and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house."
verses.34:31: They answered, "Should they have abused our sister like a prostitute?"
verses.35:1: Meanwhile God spoke to Jacob: "Rise, and go up to Bethel, and live there, and make an altar to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau."
verses.35:2: Then Jacob, having called together all his household, said, "Cast away the foreign gods that are in your midst, and purify yourselves, and change your garments.
verses.35:3: Rise, and let us go up to Bethel, so that we may make an altar there to God, who heard me in the day of my distress and was the companion of my journey."
verses.35:4: So they gave him all the foreign gods that they had and the earrings that were in their ears; and he buried them beneath the terebinth that is behind the city of Shechem.
verses.35:5: And when they had set out, the terror of God fell upon all the cities all around, and they did not dare to pursue them as they departed.
verses.35:6: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, called by the name Bethel, he himself and all the people with him.
verses.35:7: And he built an altar there, and called the name of that place House of God, for there God appeared to him when he was fleeing from his brother.
verses.35:8: At the same time Deborah, the nurse of Rebekah, died, and she was buried at the foot of Bethel beneath an oak; and the name of that place was called Oak of Weeping.
verses.35:9: Now God appeared again to Jacob after he returned from Mesopotamia of Syria, and blessed him,
verses.35:10: saying, "You will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel will be your name." And He called him Israel,
verses.35:11: and said to him, "I am God Almighty: increase and multiply; nations and peoples of nations will come from you; kings will come forth from your loins,
verses.35:12: and the land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to you and to your seed after you."
verses.35:14: Then he set up a stone pillar in the place where God had spoken to him, offering libations upon it and pouring out oil,
verses.35:15: and calling the name of that place Bethel.
verses.35:16: Having gone out from there, he came in the springtime to the land that leads to Ephrath, in which, while Rachel was in labor,
verses.35:17: because of the difficulty of childbirth, she began to be in danger. And the midwife said to her, "Do not be afraid, for you will have this son also."
verses.35:18: Now as her soul was departing because of the pain, and death was already imminent, she called the name of her son Ben-oni, that is, Son of my pain; but the father called him Benjamin, that is, Son of the right hand.
verses.35:19: So Rachel died and was buried on the road that leads to Ephrath; this is Bethlehem.
verses.35:20: And Jacob set up a pillar over her tomb; this is the pillar of Rachel's monument to the present day.
verses.35:21: Having gone out from there, he pitched his tent beyond the Tower of the Flock.
verses.35:22: And while he was living in that region, Reuben went and slept with Bilhah, his father's concubine; and this was not at all hidden from him. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.
verses.35:23: The sons of Leah: the firstborn Reuben, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun.
verses.35:24: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.35:25: The sons of Bilhah, the maidservant of Rachel: Dan and Naphtali.
verses.35:26: The sons of Zilpah, the maidservant of Leah: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.
verses.35:27: He also came to his father Isaac at Mamre, the city of Arba—this is Hebron—in which Abraham and Isaac sojourned.
verses.35:28: And the days of Isaac were completed: one hundred eighty years.
verses.35:29: And worn out by age, he died, and was joined to his people, old and full of days; and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
verses.36:1: Now these are the generations of Esau; he is Edom.
verses.36:2: Esau took wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
verses.36:3: also Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.
verses.36:4: Now Adah bore Eliphaz; Basemath gave birth to Reuel;
verses.36:5: Oholibamah brought forth Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
verses.36:6: Then Esau took his wives, his sons, and his daughters, and every soul of his household, and his property, and his livestock, and everything that he was able to possess in the land of Canaan, and he went away into another region and withdrew from his brother Jacob.
verses.36:7: For they were very rich, and they could not dwell together; nor did the land of their sojourning sustain them because of the multitude of their flocks.
verses.36:8: And Esau dwelt in Mount Seir; he is Edom.
verses.36:9: These are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in Mount Seir,
verses.36:10: and these are the names of his sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; also Reuel, the son of Basemath, his wife.
verses.36:11: And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
verses.36:12: Now Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and she bore Amalek to him. These are the sons of Adah, the wife of Esau.
verses.36:13: Now the sons of Reuel were Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah; these are the sons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
verses.36:14: These also were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the wife of Esau, whom she bore to him: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
verses.36:15: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, the firstborn of Esau: Chief Teman, Chief Omar, Chief Zepho, Chief Kenaz,
verses.36:16: Chief Korah, Chief Gatam, Chief Amalek. These are the sons of Eliphaz in the land of Edom, and these are the sons of Adah.
verses.36:17: These also are the sons of Reuel, the son of Esau: Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, Chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
verses.36:18: Now these are the sons of Oholibamah, the wife of Esau: Chief Jeush, Chief Jalam, Chief Korah. These are the chiefs of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the wife of Esau.
verses.36:19: These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs; he is Edom.
verses.36:20: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
verses.36:21: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the Horite chiefs, the sons of Seir in the land of Edom.
verses.36:22: Now the sons of Lotan were Hori and Heman; and the sister of Lotan was Timna.
verses.36:23: And these are the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
verses.36:24: And these are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is Anah, who found warm waters in the wilderness while pasturing the donkeys of Zibeon his father;
verses.36:25: and he had a son, Dishon, and a daughter, Oholibamah.
verses.36:26: And these are the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
verses.36:27: These also are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
verses.36:28: Now Dishan had sons: Uz and Aram.
verses.36:29: These are the chiefs of the Horites: Chief Lotan, Chief Shobal, Chief Zibeon, Chief Anah,
verses.36:30: Chief Dishon, Chief Ezer, Chief Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites who ruled in the land of Seir.
verses.36:31: Now the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before the sons of Israel had a king were these:
verses.36:32: Bela the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
verses.36:33: Then Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah, from Bozrah, reigned in his place.
verses.36:34: And when Jobab had died, Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
verses.36:35: When he also had died, Hadad the son of Bedad, who struck down Midian in the region of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.
verses.36:36: And when Hadad had died, Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
verses.36:37: When he also had died, Shaul from the river Rehoboth reigned in his place.
verses.36:38: And when he also had passed away, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor succeeded to the kingdom.
verses.36:39: When he also had died, Hadar reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Pau; and his wife was called Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
verses.36:40: Therefore these are the names of the chiefs of Esau in their clans, places, and designations: Chief Timna, Chief Alvah, Chief Jetheth,
verses.36:41: Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
verses.36:42: Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar,
verses.36:43: Chief Magdiel, Chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, dwelling in the land of their dominion; he is Esau, the father of the Edomites.
verses.37:1: Now Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, in which his father sojourned.
verses.37:2: And these are his generations: Joseph, when he was sixteen years old, was tending the flock with his brothers, still a boy; and he was with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father's wives, and he accused his brothers before his father of a most wicked crime.
verses.37:3: Now Israel loved Joseph above all his sons, because he had fathered him in old age; and he made for him a multicolored tunic.
verses.37:4: Now when his brothers saw that he was loved by his father more than all the sons, they hated him and could not speak anything peaceful to him.
verses.37:5: It also happened that he reported to his brothers a dream he had seen, and this matter was a seedbed of greater hatred.
verses.37:6: And he said to them, "Listen to my dream that I saw:
verses.37:7: I thought that we were binding sheaves in the field, and that my sheaf, as it were, rose up and stood, and that your sheaves, standing around, paid homage to my sheaf."
verses.37:8: His brothers answered, "Will you really be our king? Or will we be subjected to your dominion?" Therefore this matter of the dreams and words supplied fuel for envy and hatred.
verses.37:9: He also saw another dream, and recounting it to his brothers, he said, "I saw in a dream, as it were, the sun and the moon and eleven stars paying homage to me."
verses.37:10: When he had reported this to his father and brothers, his father rebuked him and said, "What does this dream that you saw mean? Will I and your mother and your brothers really pay homage to you upon the earth?"
verses.37:11: Therefore his brothers envied him, but his father silently considered the matter.
verses.37:12: And when his brothers were staying in Shechem, tending their father's flocks,
verses.37:13: Israel said to him, "Your brothers are tending the sheep in Shechem; come, I will send you to them." When he answered,
verses.37:14: "I am ready." He said to him, "Go and see whether all things are well with your brothers and the livestock, and report back to me what is going on." Having been sent from the valley of Hebron, he came to Shechem,
verses.37:15: and a man found him wandering in the field and asked what he was looking for.
verses.37:16: And he answered, "I am looking for my brothers; tell me where they are tending the flocks."
verses.37:17: And the man said to him, "They have departed from this place, and I heard them saying, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went on after his brothers and found them in Dothan.
verses.37:18: When they saw him from a distance, before he came near to them, they planned to kill him,
verses.37:19: and they were speaking to one another, "Look, the dreamer is coming;
verses.37:20: come, let us kill him and throw him into an old cistern, and we will say, 'A most vicious wild animal has devoured him,' and then it will appear what his dreams profit him."
verses.37:21: Hearing this, Reuben tried to free him from their hands and said,
verses.37:22: "Do not take his life, and do not shed blood; rather, throw him into this cistern, which is in the wilderness, and keep your hands innocent." Now he said this, wishing to rescue him from their hands and return him to his father.
verses.37:23: Therefore, immediately when he reached his brothers, they stripped him of the ankle-length and multicolored tunic,
verses.37:24: and put him into the old cistern, which had no water.
verses.37:25: And sitting down to eat bread, they saw Ishmaelite travelers coming from Gilead, and their camels carrying spices and resin and stacte into Egypt.
verses.37:26: Therefore Judah said to his brothers, "What does it profit us if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
verses.37:27: It is better that he be sold to the Ishmaelites and that our hands not be defiled, for he is our brother and our flesh." The brothers agreed with his words.
verses.37:28: And as Midianite merchants were passing by, drawing him out of the cistern, they sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver, who led him into Egypt.
verses.37:29: And Reuben, returning to the cistern, did not find the boy,
verses.37:30: and having torn his clothes, going to his brothers, he said, "The boy is not to be found, and where will I go?"
verses.37:31: Now they took his tunic and dipped it in the blood of a young goat that they had killed,
verses.37:32: sending some to carry it to their father and say, "We found this; see whether it is your son's tunic or not."
verses.37:33: When his father recognized it, he said, "It is my son's tunic; a most vicious wild animal has eaten him, a beast has devoured Joseph."
verses.37:34: And having torn his clothes, he put on sackcloth, mourning his son for a long time.
verses.37:35: Now when all his children had gathered together to soothe their father's grief, he refused to accept consolation and said, "I will go down to my son mourning into the underworld." And while he persisted in weeping,
verses.37:36: the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, commander of the army.
verses.38:1: At that time, Judah, going down from his brothers, turned aside to an Adullamite man named Hirah.
verses.38:2: And there he saw the daughter of a Canaanite man called Shua; and having taken her as wife, he went in to her.
verses.38:3: She conceived and bore a son, and called his name Er.
verses.38:4: Having conceived a child again, she named the son who was born Onan.
verses.38:5: She also bore a third, whom she called Shelah; and after he was born, she ceased to give birth any further.
verses.38:6: Now Judah gave a wife to his firstborn Er, named Tamar.
verses.38:7: And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the Lord, and he was killed by Him.
verses.38:8: Therefore Judah said to Onan his son, "Go in to your brother's wife, and be united to her, so that you may raise up seed for your brother."
verses.38:9: He, knowing that the sons would not be born for himself, when going in to his brother's wife, poured out the seed on the ground, so that children would not be born in his brother's name.
verses.38:10: And for this reason the Lord struck him down, because he was doing a detestable thing.
verses.38:11: For this reason Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Be a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up." For he was afraid that he too might die, like his brothers. And she went away and lived in her father's house.
verses.38:12: Now after many days had passed, the daughter of Shua, Judah's wife, died; and he, having received consolation after mourning, was going up to the shearers of his sheep, he and Hirah the Adullamite, shepherd of the flock, to Timnah.
verses.38:13: And it was reported to Tamar that her father-in-law was going up to Timnah to shear the sheep.
verses.38:14: Having laid aside the garments of widowhood, she put on a veil; and having changed her attire, she sat at the fork of the road that leads to Timnah, because Shelah had grown up and she had not received him as a husband.
verses.38:15: When Judah saw her, he suspected she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face so that she would not be recognized.
verses.38:16: And approaching her, he said, "Allow me to lie with you," for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. When she answered, "What will you give me so that you may enjoy lying with me?"
verses.38:17: he said, "I will send you a young goat from the flocks." And when she said again, "I will permit what you want, if you give me a pledge until you send what you promise,"
verses.38:18: Judah said, "What do you want to be given to you as a pledge?" She answered, "Your ring and bracelet, and the staff that you hold in your hand." Therefore at a single union the woman conceived,
verses.38:19: and rising up, she went away; and having laid aside the attire that she had put on, she put on the garments of widowhood.
verses.38:20: Now Judah sent the young goat by his Adullamite shepherd in order to recover the pledge that he had given to the woman; and when he did not find her,
verses.38:21: he asked the men of that place, "Where is the woman who was sitting at the fork in the road?" And all answered, "There has been no prostitute in this place."
verses.38:22: He returned to Judah and said to him, "I have not found her; and besides, the men of that place told me that a prostitute had never sat there."
verses.38:23: Judah said, "Let her keep it for herself; certainly she cannot accuse us of a lie. I sent the young goat that I had promised, and you did not find her."
verses.38:24: Now, after three months, they reported to Judah, saying, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has committed fornication, and her womb appears to be swelling." Judah said, "Bring her out so that she may be burned."
verses.38:25: When she was being led to punishment, she sent word to her father-in-law, saying, "By the man to whom these belong, I have conceived; recognize to whom the ring, bracelet, and staff belong."
verses.38:26: And he, having recognized the gifts, said, "She is more righteous than I, because I did not give her to my son Shelah." Yet he did not know her any further.
verses.38:27: Now when birth was at hand, twins appeared in the womb; and in the very delivery of the infants, one put out a hand, on which the midwife tied a scarlet thread, saying,
verses.38:29: But as he drew back his hand, the other came out; and the woman said, "Why has the wall been divided because of you?" And for this reason she called his name Perez.
verses.38:30: Afterward his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet thread, whom she called Zerah.
verses.39:1: Therefore Joseph was led into Egypt, and Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, commander of the army, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites by whom he had been brought.
verses.39:2: And the Lord was with him, and he was a man succeeding in all things; and he lived in the house of his master,
verses.39:3: who knew very well that the Lord was with him, and that all things that he carried out were directed by Him in his hand.
verses.39:4: And Joseph found favor before his master and served him; having been placed over all things by him, he governed the house entrusted to him and everything that had been handed over to him.
verses.39:5: And the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian because of Joseph, and He multiplied all his possessions, both in the house and in the fields;
verses.39:6: nor did he know anything else except the bread that he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in face and pleasing in appearance.
verses.39:7: Now after many days, his mistress cast her eyes on Joseph and said, "Sleep with me."
verses.39:8: He, by no means consenting to the wicked deed, said to her, "Look, my master, with all things handed over to me, does not know what he has in his house,
verses.39:9: nor is there anything that is not in my power or that he has not handed over to me, except you, who are his wife. How then can I do this evil and sin against my God?"
verses.39:10: With words of this kind, day by day, the woman was troublesome to the young man, yet he refused defilement.
verses.39:11: Now it happened that on a certain day Joseph entered the house and was doing some work without witnesses,
verses.39:12: and she, having seized the hem of his garment, said, "Sleep with me." Leaving his cloak in her hand, he fled and went outside.
verses.39:13: And when the woman saw the garment in her hands and that she had been scorned,
verses.39:14: she called to herself the men of her house and said to them, "Look, he has brought in a Hebrew man to mock us; he came in to me to lie with me, and when I cried out
verses.39:15: and he heard my voice, he left the cloak that I was holding and fled outside."
verses.39:16: Therefore, as proof of credibility, she showed the cloak she had kept to her husband returning home,
verses.39:17: and said, "The Hebrew slave whom you brought came in to me to mock me;
verses.39:18: and when he heard me crying out, he left the cloak that I was holding and fled outside."
verses.39:19: Having heard these things, and being overly credulous of the words of his wife, the master became very angry;
verses.39:20: and he handed Joseph over into the prison where the prisoners of the king were guarded, and he was confined there.
