verses.39:21: Now the Lord was with Joseph, and having had mercy on him, He gave him favor in the sight of the chief of the prison.
verses.39:22: He handed over into his hand all the prisoners who were held in custody, and whatever was done was under him.
verses.39:23: Nor did he know anything, with all things entrusted to him; for the Lord was with him, and He directed all his works.
verses.40:1: After these things had thus taken place, it happened that two eunuchs, the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker, sinned against their master.
verses.40:2: And Pharaoh, being angry against them (for one was over the cupbearers, the other over the bakers),
verses.40:3: sent them into the prison of the commander of the soldiers, where Joseph also was bound.
verses.40:4: Now the keeper of the prison handed them over to Joseph, who also served them; some time had passed, and they were held in custody.
verses.40:5: And both saw a dream in one night, according to an interpretation fitting for them.
verses.40:6: When Joseph came in to them in the morning and saw that they were sad,
verses.40:7: he inquired, saying, "Why is your face sadder today than usual?"
verses.40:8: They answered, "We have seen a dream, and there is no one to interpret it for us." And Joseph said to them, "Does not interpretation belong to God? Tell me what you have seen."
verses.40:9: First, the overseer of the cupbearers related his dream: "I saw before me a vine,
verses.40:10: on which there were three shoots, with buds gradually growing, and after the blossoms, grapes ripening,
verses.40:11: and Pharaoh's cup in my hand. So I took the grapes and pressed them into the cup that I was holding, and handed the cup to Pharaoh."
verses.40:12: Joseph answered, "This is the interpretation of the dream: the three shoots are three more days,
verses.40:13: after which Pharaoh will remember your office and will restore you to your former rank; and you will give him the cup according to your duty, just as you were accustomed to do before.
verses.40:14: Only remember me when it is well with you, and show mercy to me, so that you may speak to Pharaoh and he may bring me out of this prison;
verses.40:15: for I was carried off by theft from the land of the Hebrews, and here, innocent, I was cast into the pit."
verses.40:16: Seeing that he had wisely solved the dream, the master of the bakers said, "I too saw a dream: that I had three baskets of flour on my head,
verses.40:17: and in one basket that was uppermost, I was carrying all the foods that are made by the baker's craft, and birds were eating from it."
verses.40:18: Joseph answered, "This is the interpretation of the dream: the three baskets are three more days,
verses.40:19: after which Pharaoh will take away your head and will hang you on a cross, and the birds will tear your flesh."
verses.40:20: After that, the third day was Pharaoh's birthday; and making a great banquet for his servants, he remembered the master of the cupbearers and the chief of the bakers during the feast.
verses.40:21: And he restored the one to his place, so that he might hand the cup to him;
verses.40:22: the other he hanged on a gallows, so that the truth of the dream interpreter might be proved.
verses.40:23: Nevertheless, with prosperity following, the overseer of the cupbearers forgot his interpreter.
verses.41:1: After two years, Pharaoh saw a dream. He thought he was standing by the river,
verses.41:2: out of which seven cows were coming up, beautiful and exceedingly fat, and they were grazing in marshy places.
verses.41:3: Seven others also were emerging from the river, ugly and wasted with emaciation, and they were grazing on the very bank of the river in green places;
verses.41:4: and they devoured those whose appearance and bodily condition were remarkable. Having woken up, Pharaoh
verses.41:5: slept again and saw a second dream: seven heads of grain were sprouting on one stalk, full and lovely.
verses.41:6: Just as many other heads of grain also, thin and struck by blight, were springing up,
verses.41:7: devouring the beauty of all the former ones. When Pharaoh woke up after rest,
verses.41:8: and when morning came, terrified with dread, he sent for all the diviners of Egypt and all the wise men; and when they had been summoned, he told them the dream, and there was no one who could interpret it.
verses.41:9: Then at last, remembering, the master of the cupbearers said, "I confess my sin:
verses.41:10: when the king was angry with his servants, he ordered me and the master of the bakers to be thrust into the prison of the commander of the soldiers,
verses.41:11: where on one night each of us saw a dream foretelling things to come.
verses.41:12: There was a Hebrew youth there, a servant of that same captain of the soldiers; and when we told him the dreams,
verses.41:13: we heard whatever the outcome of the matter afterward proved; for I was restored to my office, and he was hanged on a cross."
verses.41:14: Immediately, at the king's command, they brought Joseph out of prison and shaved him; and when his clothing had been changed, they presented him to him.
verses.41:15: He said to him, "I have seen dreams, and there is no one who can explain them; I have heard that you interpret them most wisely."
verses.41:16: Joseph answered, "Apart from me, God will give a favorable answer to Pharaoh."
verses.41:17: Therefore Pharaoh recounted what he had seen: "I thought I was standing on the bank of the river,
verses.41:18: and seven cows were coming up out of the river, exceedingly beautiful and fat in flesh, which were cropping the greenery in the pasture of the marsh.
verses.41:19: And look, seven other cows were following these, so deformed and emaciated that I have never seen such ones in the land of Egypt;
verses.41:20: which, after devouring and consuming the former ones,
verses.41:21: gave no trace of fullness, but remained sluggish in similar emaciation and squalor. Waking up, and again weighed down by deep sleep,
verses.41:22: I saw a dream. Seven heads of grain were sprouting on one stalk, full and very beautiful.
verses.41:23: Seven others also, thin and struck by blight, were springing up from the stalk,
verses.41:24: which devoured the beauty of the former ones. I told the dream to the diviners, and there is no one who can explain it."
verses.41:25: Joseph answered, "The king's dream is one: God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
verses.41:26: The seven beautiful cows and the seven full heads of grain are seven years of plenty, and they contain the same meaning of the dream.
verses.41:27: Also the seven thin and emaciated cows that came up after them, and the seven thin heads of grain struck by a scorching wind, are seven years of coming famine.
verses.41:28: These will be fulfilled in this order:
verses.41:29: look, seven years of great fertility will come in the entire land of Egypt,
verses.41:30: and seven other years of such barrenness will follow them that all the former abundance will be handed over to oblivion; for the famine will consume the whole land,
verses.41:31: and the greatness of the scarcity will destroy the greatness of the plenty.
verses.41:32: Now as for the fact that you saw a dream a second time pertaining to the same matter, it is a sign of certainty, because the word of God is coming to pass and will be fulfilled very swiftly.
verses.41:33: Now therefore, let the king look out for a wise and industrious man and set him over the land of Egypt,
verses.41:34: who shall appoint overseers throughout all the regions, and a fifth part of the produce during the seven years of fertility
verses.41:35: that are now about to come, let him gather into granaries; and let all the grain be stored under Pharaoh's authority and kept in the cities.
verses.41:36: And let it be prepared for the coming seven-year famine that will afflict Egypt, and the land will not be consumed by scarcity."
verses.41:37: The counsel pleased Pharaoh and all his ministers;
verses.41:38: and he spoke to them, "Will we be able to find such a man, who is full of the spirit of God?"
verses.41:39: Therefore he said to Joseph, "Since God has shown you all that you have spoken, will I be able to find anyone wiser and like you?
verses.41:40: You will be over my house, and all the people will obey at the command of your mouth; by the throne of the kingdom alone will I precede you."
verses.41:41: And Pharaoh said again to Joseph, "Look, I have appointed you over the entire land of Egypt," and
verses.41:42: took the ring from his hand and put it on his hand; and he clothed him with a robe of fine linen and placed a gold chain around his neck.
verses.41:43: And he had him mount his second chariot, while a herald cried out that all should bend the knee before him and know that he was set over the entire land of Egypt.
verses.41:44: The king also said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh: without your command, no one will move hand or foot in all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:45: And he changed his name and called him, in the Egyptian language, Savior of the world. He also gave him as wife Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis. So Joseph, having gone out to the land of Egypt
verses.41:46: (now he was thirty years old when he stood in the presence of King Pharaoh), went around all the regions of Egypt.
verses.41:47: And the fertility of the seven years came, and the crops, brought into sheaves, were gathered into the granaries of Egypt.
verses.41:48: Also all the abundance of produce was stored in each city.
verses.41:49: And so great was the quantity of wheat that it was equal to the sand of the sea, and the supply exceeded measure.
verses.41:50: Now two sons were born to Joseph before the famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him.
verses.41:51: And he called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, saying, "God has made me forget all my labors and my father's house."
verses.41:52: He also called the name of the second Ephraim, saying, "God has made me grow in the land of my poverty."
verses.41:53: Therefore, when the seven years of plenty that had been in Egypt had passed,
verses.41:54: the seven years of scarcity that Joseph had foretold began to come; and in the entire world the famine prevailed, and in the whole land of Egypt there was bread.
verses.41:55: When that land grew hungry, the people cried out to Pharaoh, asking for food. He answered them, "Go to Joseph, and do whatever he tells you."
verses.41:56: Now the famine was growing daily in all the land, and Joseph opened all the granaries and kept selling to the Egyptians, for the famine had oppressed them as well.
verses.41:57: And all the provinces were coming into Egypt to buy provisions and relieve the evil of scarcity.
verses.42:1: Now Jacob, hearing that provisions were being sold in Egypt, said to his sons, "Why are you negligent?
verses.42:2: I have heard that wheat is being sold in Egypt. Go down and buy necessities for us, so that we may be able to live and not be consumed by scarcity."
verses.42:3: Therefore ten brothers of Joseph, going down to buy grain in Egypt,
verses.42:4: with Benjamin kept at home by Jacob, who had said to his brothers, "For fear that he might suffer any harm on the journey,"
verses.42:5: entered the land of Egypt with others who were going to buy. Now there was famine in the land of Canaan.
verses.42:6: And Joseph was ruler in the land of Egypt, and at his command grain was sold to the peoples. And when his brothers had paid homage to him,
verses.42:7: and he had recognized them, he spoke rather harshly, as if to strangers, questioning them, "Where have you come from?" And they answered, "From the land of Canaan, so that we may buy necessities for sustenance."
verses.42:8: And yet, recognizing his brothers himself, he was not recognized by them.
verses.42:9: And remembering the dreams that he had once seen, he said to them, "You are spies. You have come to see the weaker parts of the land."
verses.42:10: They said, "It is not so, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
verses.42:11: All of us are sons of one man. We have come as peaceful men, and your servants are plotting nothing evil."
verses.42:12: He answered them, "It is otherwise. You have come to inspect the unfortified parts of this land."
verses.42:13: And they said, "We, your servants, are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is with our father, and the other is no more."
verses.42:14: "This," he said, "is what I have spoken: you are spies.
verses.42:15: Right now I will put you to the test: by the health of Pharaoh, you will not depart from here until your youngest brother comes.
verses.42:16: Send one of you, and let him bring him, while you will be in bonds until the things you have said are tested, whether they are true or false; otherwise, by the health of Pharaoh, you are spies."
verses.42:17: Therefore he handed them over to custody for three days.
verses.42:18: Now on the third day, when they had been brought out of prison, he said, "Do what I have said, and you will live, for I fear God.
verses.42:19: If you are peaceful men, let one brother of yours be bound in prison, while you go away and carry the grain that you have bought to your houses,
verses.42:20: and bring your youngest brother to me, so that I may be able to test your words, and you may not die." They did as he had said,
verses.42:21: and they spoke to one another, "Deservedly we suffer these things, because we sinned against our brother, seeing the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. For that reason this tribulation has come upon us."
verses.42:22: One of them, Reuben, said, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not sin against the boy,' and you did not listen to me? Look, his blood is being demanded."
verses.42:23: Now they did not know that Joseph understood, because he was speaking to them through an interpreter.
verses.42:24: And he turned himself away for a little while and wept; and returning, he spoke to them.
verses.42:25: Taking Simeon and binding him in their presence, he commanded his attendants to fill their sacks with wheat and to put back each one's money in their bags, with provisions given in addition for the journey; and they did so.
verses.42:26: Then they, carrying the grain on their donkeys, set out.
verses.42:27: And when one of them had opened his sack to give fodder to his pack animal at the lodging place, observing the money in the mouth of the bag,
verses.42:28: he said to his brothers, "The money has been returned to me; look, it is found in the sack." And astonished and troubled, they said to one another, "What is this that God has done to us?"
verses.42:29: And they came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, and reported to him all the things that had happened to them, saying,
verses.42:30: "The lord of the land spoke harshly to us, and thought us spies of the province.
verses.42:31: We answered him, 'We are peaceful men, and we are devising no plots.
verses.42:32: We are twelve brothers born of one father; one is no more, and the youngest stays with our father in the land of Canaan.'
verses.42:33: And he said to us, 'In this way I will test that you are peaceful men: leave one brother of yours with me, and take the provisions necessary for your houses, and go away,
verses.42:34: and bring your youngest brother to me, so that I may know that you are not spies, and that you may be able to receive back this one who is held in bonds, and from then on have permission to buy what you wish.'"
verses.42:35: When these things had been said, as they were pouring out the grain, each one found money tied up in the mouth of the sacks; and with all of them terrified together,
verses.42:36: their father Jacob said, "You have made me to be without children: Joseph is no more, Simeon is held in bonds, and you will take Benjamin away; all these evils have fallen upon me."
verses.42:37: To whom Reuben answered, "Kill my two sons if I do not bring him back to you. Hand him over into my hand, and I myself will restore him to you."
verses.42:38: But he said, "My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he alone has remained. If anything adverse happens to him in the land to which you are going, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the underworld."
verses.43:1: Meanwhile the famine was pressing severely upon the whole land.
verses.43:2: And when the food that they had brought from Egypt had been consumed, Jacob said to his sons, "Return, and buy a little food for us."
verses.43:3: Judah answered, "That man solemnly warned us under the testimony of an oath, saying, 'You will not see my face unless you bring your youngest brother with you.'
verses.43:4: Therefore if you are willing to send him with us, we will go together and buy necessities for you;
verses.43:5: but if you are not willing, we will not go, for the man, as we have often said, solemnly warned us, saying, 'You will not see my face without your youngest brother.'"
verses.43:6: Israel said to them, "You have done this to my misery, by telling him that you also had another brother."
verses.43:7: And they answered, "The man questioned us in order about our family: whether our father was alive, whether we had a brother; and we answered him accordingly, in keeping with what he had inquired. Could we possibly know that he was going to say, 'Bring your brother with you'?"
verses.43:8: Judah also said to his father, "Send the boy with me, so that we may set out and be able to live, so that we and our little ones may not die.
verses.43:9: I myself take charge of the boy; require him from my hand. Unless I bring him back and hand him over to you, I will be guilty of a sin against you for all time.
verses.43:10: If delay had not intervened, we would already have come a second time."
verses.43:11: Therefore their father Israel said to them, "If it must be so, do what you wish: take some of the best fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry gifts down to the man: a little resin, and honey, and storax, and stacte, and terebinth, and almonds.
verses.43:12: And carry double the money with you, and take back that which you found in the bags, in case perhaps it was done by mistake.
verses.43:13: Take your brother as well, and go to the man.
verses.43:14: And may my Almighty God make him favorable toward you, and send back with you your brother whom he holds, and this Benjamin; as for me, I will be as one bereaved, without children."
verses.43:15: Therefore the men took the gifts, and double the money, and Benjamin; and they went down into Egypt and stood before Joseph.
verses.43:16: When he had seen them and Benjamin together, he commanded the steward of his house, saying, "Bring the men into the house, and slaughter animals, and prepare a banquet, since they are going to eat with me at noon."
verses.43:17: He did what had been commanded him, and brought the men into the house.
verses.43:18: And terrified there, they said to one another, "Because of the money that we carried back earlier in our sacks, we have been brought in, so that he may cast a false accusation down upon us and violently subject both us and our donkeys to servitude."
verses.43:19: For this reason, approaching the steward of the house at the very doors,
verses.43:20: they spoke, "We beg you, my lord, to hear us. We already came down before to buy food;
verses.43:21: and when it had been bought, after we had come to the lodging place, we opened our sacks and found the money in the mouth of the sacks, which we have now brought back in the same weight.
verses.43:22: And we have also brought other silver so that we may buy what is necessary for us. It is not within our knowledge who put it in our pouches."
verses.43:23: And he answered, "Peace be with you; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasures in your bags, for I myself have the money that you gave me, verified." And he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.43:24: And when they had been brought into the house, he brought water, and they washed their feet, and he gave fodder to their donkeys.
verses.43:25: And they were preparing the gifts until Joseph should enter at noon, for they had heard that they were going to eat bread there.
verses.43:26: Therefore Joseph entered his house, and they presented the gifts to him, holding them in their hands, and paid homage, face down to the ground.
verses.43:27: And he, having kindly returned their greeting, asked them, saying, "Is your old father well, about whom you had spoken to me? Is he still alive?"
verses.43:28: And they answered, "Your servant our father is safe and well; he is still alive." And bowing low, they paid homage to him.
verses.43:29: Now Joseph, lifting up his eyes, saw Benjamin, his brother from the same womb, and said, "Is this your little brother, about whom you had spoken to me?" And again he said, "May God have mercy on you, my son."
verses.43:30: And he hurried, because his innermost being had been stirred over his brother, and tears were bursting forth; and entering the chamber, he wept.
verses.43:31: And again, having washed his face, he came out, restrained himself, and said, "Set out the loaves."
verses.43:32: When these had been set out, separately for Joseph, and separately for the brothers, and also separately for the Egyptians who were eating at the same time (for it is unlawful for Egyptians to eat with Hebrews, and they consider a banquet of this kind profane),
verses.43:33: they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his age. And they marveled exceedingly,
verses.43:34: having taken the portions that they had received from him; and a greater portion came to Benjamin, so that it exceeded by five portions. And they drank and became drunk with him.
verses.44:1: Now Joseph commanded the steward of his house, saying, "Fill their sacks with grain, as much as they can hold, and put each one's money at the top of the sack.
verses.44:2: And put my silver cup, and the price that he gave for the wheat, in the mouth of the youngest one's sack." And it was done so.
verses.44:3: And when morning dawned, they were sent away with their donkeys.
verses.44:4: And they had already gone out of the city and had gone a little way ahead; then Joseph, having summoned the steward of the house, said, "Rise, pursue the men, and when you overtake them, say, 'Why have you repaid evil for good?
verses.44:5: The cup that you stole is the very one from which my lord drinks, and in which he is accustomed to practice divination; you have done a most evil thing.'"
verses.44:6: He did as he had commanded, and when he overtook them, he spoke to them in order.
verses.44:7: They answered, "Why does our lord speak in this way, that your servants should have committed so great a crime?
verses.44:8: The money that we found at the top of the sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan; and how does it follow that we should have stolen gold or silver from your lord's house?
verses.44:9: With whichever of your servants what you seek is found, let him die, and we will be servants of our lord."
verses.44:10: He said to them, "Let it be according to your judgment: the one with whom it is found, let him be my servant, but you will be innocent."
verses.44:11: Therefore, hastily lowering their sacks to the ground, each one opened his.
verses.44:12: Having searched them, beginning from the oldest down to the youngest, he found the cup in Benjamin's sack.
verses.44:13: Then they, having torn their garments and loaded their donkeys again, returned into the town.
verses.44:14: And Judah first, with his brothers, went in to Joseph (for he had not yet departed from the place), and all of them fell down together on the ground before him.
verses.44:15: He said to them, "Why did you wish to act in this way? Or are you unaware that there is no one like me in the knowledge of divination?"
verses.44:16: Judah said to him, "What shall we answer my lord? Or what shall we speak, or what will we justly be able to put forward? God has found the iniquity of your servants; look, we are all servants of my lord, both we and the one with whom the cup was found."
verses.44:17: Joseph answered, "Far be it from me to act in this way: the one who stole the cup, let him be my servant; but you, go away free to your father."
verses.44:18: Drawing nearer, Judah said confidently, "I beg you, my lord, let your servant speak a word in your ears, and do not be angry with your servant; for you are, after Pharaoh,
verses.44:19: my lord. You asked your servants earlier, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'
verses.44:20: And we answered you, my lord, 'We have an old father, and a little boy who was born in his old age, whose brother from the same mother is dead; and his mother has him alone, while his father loves him tenderly.'
verses.44:21: And you said to your servants, 'Bring him to me, and I will set my eyes upon him.'
verses.44:22: We pointed out to my lord, 'The boy cannot leave his father, for if he leaves him, he will die.'
verses.44:23: And you said to your servants, 'Unless your youngest brother comes with you, you will not see my face again.'
verses.44:24: Therefore, when we had gone up to your servant our father, we recounted to him everything that my lord spoke.
verses.44:25: And our father said, 'Go back and buy us a little wheat.'
verses.44:26: We said to him, 'We cannot go; if our youngest brother goes down with us, we will set out together; otherwise, with him absent, we do not dare to see the man's face.'
verses.44:27: And he answered, 'You know that my wife bore two to me.
verses.44:28: One went out, and you said, "A beast has devoured him," and until now he has not appeared.
verses.44:29: If you take this one also, and anything happens to him on the way, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the underworld.'
verses.44:30: Therefore, if I go in to your servant our father, and the boy is missing (since his soul depends on this one's soul),
verses.44:31: and he sees that he is not with us, he will die, and your servants will bring down his gray hairs with grief to the underworld.
verses.44:32: I personally am your servant who received this one into my trust and gave my pledge, saying, 'Unless I bring him back, I will be guilty of sin against my father for all time.'
verses.44:33: Therefore I, your servant, will remain in place of the boy in the service of my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
verses.44:34: For I cannot return to my father with the boy absent, so that I may not be present as a witness of the calamity that is about to overwhelm my father."
verses.45:1: Joseph could no longer restrain himself with many standing by in his presence; therefore he commanded that all go outside, and that no outsider be present at their mutual recognition.
verses.45:2: And he raised his voice with weeping, which the Egyptians heard, and all the house of Pharaoh.
verses.45:3: And he said to his brothers, "I am Joseph; is my father still alive?" And the brothers could not answer, terrified with overwhelming fear.
verses.45:4: To them he said kindly, "Come near to me." And when they had come near, he said, "I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.45:5: Do not be terrified, nor let it seem hard to you that you sold me into these regions; for God sent me before you into Egypt for your preservation.
verses.45:6: It has been two years since famine began to be in the land, and five years still remain in which it will be possible neither to plow nor to reap.
verses.45:7: And God sent me ahead so that you may be preserved upon the earth, and may be able to have food to live.
verses.45:8: I was sent here not by your counsel, but by the will of God, who made me like a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler in all the land of Egypt.
verses.45:9: Hurry and go up to my father, and say to him, 'Your son Joseph sends this message: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down to me, do not delay,
verses.45:10: and you will dwell in the land of Goshen; and you will be near me, you and your sons and the sons of your sons, your sheep and herds, and everything that you possess;
verses.45:11: and there I will feed you (for five years of famine still remain), so that you may not perish, you and your house and everything that you possess.'
verses.45:12: Look, your eyes, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, see that my mouth is speaking to you.
verses.45:13: Report to my father all my glory, and everything that you have seen in Egypt; hurry, and bring him to me."
verses.45:14: And when he had embraced him and fallen upon the neck of his brother Benjamin, he wept, while he also wept likewise upon his neck.
verses.45:15: And Joseph kissed all his brothers and wept over each one; afterward they dared to speak to him.
verses.45:16: And it was heard, and spread abroad by widespread report in the king's court, "Joseph's brothers have come." And Pharaoh rejoiced, and all his household.
verses.45:17: And he told Joseph to command his brothers, saying, "Loading your pack animals, go into the land of Canaan,
verses.45:18: and take from there your father and your relatives, and come to me; and I will give you all the good things of Egypt, so that you may eat the marrow of the land.
verses.45:19: Command also that they take wagons from the land of Egypt for the transport of their little ones and wives, and say, 'Take your father, and hurry, coming as quickly as possible.
verses.45:20: Do not leave behind anything of your household goods, because all the riches of Egypt will be yours.'"
verses.45:21: And the sons of Israel did as had been commanded them. Joseph gave them wagons, according to Pharaoh's command, and provisions for the journey.
verses.45:22: And for each one he ordered two robes to be brought out; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver with five of the finest robes,
verses.45:23: sending the same amount of money and clothing to his father, adding also ten donkeys to carry some of all the riches of Egypt, and just as many female donkeys carrying wheat and bread for the journey.
verses.45:24: Therefore he sent his brothers away, and as they set out he said, "Do not be angry on the way."
verses.45:25: Going up from Egypt, they came into the land of Canaan to their father Jacob.
verses.45:26: And they reported to him, saying, "Joseph your son is alive, and he himself rules in all the land of Egypt." Having heard this, Jacob, as if waking from a heavy sleep, still did not believe them.
verses.45:27: They in reply recounted the whole sequence of the matter. And when he had seen the wagons and everything that he had sent, his spirit revived,
verses.45:28: and he said, "It is enough for me if my son Joseph is still alive; I will go and see him before I die."
verses.46:1: And Israel set out with all that he had and came to the Well of the Oath; and after sacrificing victims there to the God of his father Isaac,
verses.46:2: he heard Him through a vision of the night calling him and saying to him, "Jacob, Jacob." To Him he answered, "Here I am."
verses.46:3: God said to him, "I am the most mighty God of your father; do not be afraid, go down into Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
verses.46:4: I will go down with you there, and I will bring you from there as you return; Joseph also will place his hands upon your eyes."
verses.46:5: Jacob rose from the Well of the Oath, and his sons carried him with their little ones and their wives in the wagons that Pharaoh had sent to carry the old man,
verses.46:6: and all that he possessed in the land of Canaan; and he came into Egypt with all his seed,
verses.46:7: his sons and grandsons, his daughters, and all his descendants together.
verses.46:8: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, he himself with his children. The firstborn was Reuben.
verses.46:9: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
verses.46:10: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
verses.46:11: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.46:12: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; however, Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And sons were born to Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
verses.46:13: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Job, and Shimron.
verses.46:14: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
verses.46:15: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore in Mesopotamia of Syria, together with her daughter Dinah: all the souls of her sons and daughters were thirty-three.
verses.46:16: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
verses.46:17: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and also Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
verses.46:18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah; and she bore these to Jacob, sixteen souls.
verses.46:19: The sons of Rachel, the wife of Jacob: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.46:20: And sons were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim.
verses.46:21: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
verses.46:22: These are the sons of Rachel, whom she bore to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
verses.46:24: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
verses.46:25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel; and she bore these to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
verses.46:26: All the souls who entered Egypt with Jacob and came out from his thigh, apart from the wives of his sons, were sixty-six.
verses.46:27: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in the land of Egypt were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob who entered Egypt were seventy.
verses.46:28: Now he sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph to report to him, so that he would come to meet him in Goshen.
verses.46:29: When he had arrived there, Joseph, having harnessed his chariot, went up to meet his father at that same place; and seeing him, he threw himself upon his neck and wept amid embraces.
verses.46:30: And his father said to Joseph, "Now I will die happy, because I have seen your face and I leave you surviving."
verses.46:31: And he spoke to his brothers and to all the house of his father, "I will go up and report to Pharaoh, and I will say to him, 'My brothers and the house of my father, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me;
verses.46:32: and the men are shepherds of sheep, and they take care of raising flocks; their livestock, their herds, and all that they were able to possess, they have brought with them.'
verses.46:33: And when he calls you and says, 'What is your occupation?'
verses.46:34: you will answer, 'We, your servants, are men who are shepherds from our infancy up to the present, both we and our fathers.' Now you will say these things so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, because the Egyptians detest all shepherds of sheep."
verses.47:1: So Joseph went in and reported to Pharaoh, saying, "My father and brothers, their sheep and herds, and all that they possess have come from the land of Canaan; and look, they are staying in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:2: He also set five men, the last of his brothers, before the king,
verses.47:3: whom he asked, "What occupation do you have?" They answered, "Your servants are shepherds of sheep, both we and our fathers.
verses.47:4: We have come to sojourn in your land, since there is no grass for the flocks of your servants, as the famine grows severe in the land of Canaan; and we ask that you command us, your servants, to be in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:5: Therefore the king said to Joseph, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.
verses.47:6: The land of Egypt is before you; have them dwell in the best place, and give them the land of Goshen. And if you know that there are industrious men among them, appoint them masters of my livestock."
verses.47:7: After these things, Joseph brought his father in to the king and set him before him; and after blessing him,
verses.47:8: and being asked by him, "How many are the days of the years of your life?"
verses.47:9: he answered, "The days of my sojourning are one hundred and thirty years, few and evil, and they have not reached the days of my fathers in which they sojourned."
verses.47:10: And after blessing the king, he went outside.
verses.47:11: Now Joseph gave his father and his brothers a possession in Egypt in the best place of the land, Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.47:12: And he nourished them and all the house of his father, supplying provisions to each one.
verses.47:13: For bread was lacking in the whole world, and famine had oppressed the land, especially that of Egypt and Canaan.
verses.47:14: From them he gathered all the money for the sale of grain, and brought it into the king's treasury.
verses.47:15: And when the buyers' money to pay had run out, all Egypt came to Joseph, saying, "Give us bread; why are we dying before you now that money has run out?"
verses.47:16: To them he answered, "Bring your livestock, and I will give you food for them, if you do not have the price."
verses.47:17: When they had brought them, he gave them nourishment in exchange for horses, sheep, oxen, and donkeys; and he sustained them that year through the exchange of livestock.
verses.47:18: And they came in the second year and said to him, "We will not hide from our lord that now that money has run out, the livestock have also run out; nor is it hidden from you that apart from our bodies and our land we have nothing.
verses.47:19: Why then shall we die while you look on? Both we and our land will be yours; buy us into royal servitude and supply seed, so that the land may not be reduced to desolation as the tiller perishes."
verses.47:20: Therefore Joseph bought all the land of Egypt, as each one sold his possessions because of the severity of the famine. And he subjected it to Pharaoh,
verses.47:21: and all its peoples, from the farthest borders of Egypt to its outermost boundaries,
verses.47:22: except the land of the priests, which had been given to them by the king, to whom fixed provisions were also supplied from the public granaries; and for that reason they were not forced to sell their possessions.
verses.47:23: Therefore Joseph said to the peoples, "Look, as you see, Pharaoh possesses both you and your land; take seed and sow the fields,
verses.47:24: so that you may have crops. You will give a fifth part to the king; the remaining four I leave to you for sowing, and for food for your households and your children."
verses.47:25: And they answered, "Our preservation is in your hand; only let our lord regard us, and we will gladly serve the king."
verses.47:26: From that time up to the present day, throughout the entire land of Egypt a fifth part is paid to the kings, and it became as it were a law, apart from the priestly land, which was free from this condition.
verses.47:27: So Israel dwelt in Egypt, that is, in the land of Goshen, and he possessed it; and he increased and multiplied exceedingly.
verses.47:28: And he lived in it seventeen years; and all the days of his life came to one hundred and forty-seven years.
verses.47:29: And when he saw that the day of his death was approaching, he called his son Joseph and said to him, "If I have found favor in your sight, place your hand under my thigh, and you will show mercy and truth to me, that you not bury me in Egypt,
verses.47:30: but that I sleep with my fathers, and that you carry me away from this land and lay me in the tomb of my ancestors." To him Joseph answered, "I will do what you have commanded."
verses.47:31: And he said, "Swear to me, then." As he swore, Israel worshiped God, having turned toward the head of the bed.
verses.48:1: After these things were thus concluded, it was reported to Joseph that his father was ill; and taking his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim, he proceeded to go.
verses.48:2: And it was told to the old man, "Look, your son Joseph is coming to you." And having been strengthened, he sat up on the bed.
verses.48:3: And when he came in to him, he said, "God Almighty appeared to me in Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
verses.48:4: and said, 'I will increase and multiply you, and make you into multitudes of peoples; and I will give this land to you and to your seed after you as an everlasting possession.'
verses.48:5: Therefore your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came here to you, will be mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, just like Reuben and Simeon, will be reckoned to me.
verses.48:6: But the remaining ones whom you father after them will be yours, and they will be called by the name of their brothers in their possessions.
verses.48:7: For to me, when I was coming from Mesopotamia, Rachel died in the land of Canaan on the journey itself, and it was springtime; and I was entering Ephrath, and I buried her beside the road of Ephrath, which by another name is called Bethlehem."
verses.48:8: Now seeing his sons, he said to him, "Who are these?"
verses.48:9: He answered, "They are my sons, whom God gave me in this place." "Bring them to me," he said, "so that I may bless them."
verses.48:10: For the eyes of Israel were dim because of extreme old age, and he could not see clearly. And when they were brought near to him, having kissed and embraced them,
verses.48:11: he said to his son, "I have not been deprived of the sight of you; furthermore, God has shown me your seed."
verses.48:12: And when Joseph had taken them from his father's lap, he bowed down prostrate to the ground.
verses.48:13: And he placed Ephraim at his right hand, that is, at Israel's left, but Manasseh on his left hand, namely at his father's right, and he brought both of them near to him.
verses.48:14: And stretching out his right hand, he placed it upon the head of Ephraim, the younger brother, and his left upon the head of Manasseh, who was older by birth, crossing his hands.
verses.48:15: And Jacob blessed the sons of Joseph, and said, "The God in whose presence my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who shepherds me from my youth up to the present day,
verses.48:16: the angel who rescued me from all evils, bless these boys; and let my name be invoked upon them, and also the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and let them grow into a multitude upon the earth."
verses.48:17: Now Joseph, seeing that his father had placed his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, took it hard; and taking hold of his father's hand, he tried to lift it from the head of Ephraim and move it onto the head of Manasseh.
verses.48:18: And he said to his father, "It is not fitting this way, father; because this one is the firstborn, place your right hand upon his head."
verses.48:19: But he, refusing, said, "I know, my son, I know; this one too will indeed become peoples and will be multiplied, but his younger brother will be greater than he, and his seed will grow into nations."
verses.48:20: And he blessed them at that very time, saying, "In you Israel will be blessed, and it will be said, 'May God do for you as for Ephraim and as for Manasseh.'" And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
verses.48:21: And he said to Joseph his son, "Look, I am dying, and God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.
verses.48:22: I give you one portion beyond your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and bow."
verses.49:1: Now Jacob called his sons and said to them, "Gather together, so that I may declare what is to come to you in the last days.
verses.49:2: Gather together and listen, sons of Jacob; listen to Israel your father:
verses.49:3: Reuben, my firstborn, you are my strength and the beginning of my sorrow, foremost in gifts, greater in authority.
verses.49:4: You are poured out like water; may you not grow, because you went up to your father's bed and defiled his couch.
verses.49:5: Simeon and Levi are brothers: warring vessels of iniquity.
verses.49:6: Into their counsel let my soul not come, and in their assembly let my glory not be; because in their fury they killed a man, and in their own will they undermined a wall.
verses.49:7: Cursed be their fury, because it is stubborn, and their indignation, because it is harsh; I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.
verses.49:8: Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hand will be upon the necks of your enemies; the sons of your father will bow down to you.
verses.49:9: A lion's cub is Judah; to the prey, my son, you have gone up; resting, you lay down like a lion, and like a lioness; who will rouse him?
verses.49:10: The scepter will not be removed from Judah, nor a leader from his thigh, until the one who is to be sent comes, and he himself will be the expectation of the nations.
verses.49:11: Tying his foal to the vineyard, and to the vine, my son, his female donkey, he will wash his robe in wine and his cloak in the blood of the grape.
verses.49:12: His eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.
verses.49:13: Zebulun will dwell on the shore of the sea, and in the harbor of ships, extending as far as Sidon.
verses.49:14: Issachar is a strong donkey lying down between the borders.
verses.49:15: And he saw rest, that it was good, and the land, that it was the best; and he submitted his shoulder to carrying, and became a servant to tributes.
verses.49:16: Dan will judge his people just like another tribe in Israel.
verses.49:17: Let Dan be a snake in the road, a horned viper in the path, biting the hooves of the horse so that its rider falls backward.
verses.49:18: I will wait for Your salvation, Lord.
verses.49:19: Gad, girded, will fight before him, and he himself will be girded behind.
verses.49:20: Asher, his bread is rich, and he will provide delicacies for kings.
verses.49:21: Naphtali is a stag let loose and giving words of beauty.
verses.49:22: Joseph is a growing son, a growing son and handsome in appearance; the daughters ran about upon the wall.
verses.49:23: But they provoked him and quarreled, and those with javelins envied him.
verses.49:24: His bow rested in strength, and the bonds of his arms and hands were loosed through the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there the shepherd came forth, the stone of Israel.
verses.49:25: The God of your father will be your helper, and the Almighty will bless you with blessings of heaven from above, with blessings of the deep lying below, with blessings of the breasts and of the womb.
verses.49:26: The blessings of your father have been strengthened by the blessings of his fathers, until the desire of the eternal hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the head of the Nazirite among his brothers.
verses.49:27: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he will eat the prey, and in the evening he will divide the spoils."
verses.49:28: All these are in the twelve tribes of Israel; these things their father spoke to them, and he blessed each one with their own blessings.
verses.49:29: And he commanded them, saying, "I am being gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the double cave which is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
verses.49:30: opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as the possession of a burial place.
verses.49:31: There they buried him and Sarah his wife; there Isaac was buried with Rebekah his spouse; and there Leah also lies buried."
verses.49:32: And when the commands with which he was instructing his sons were finished, he drew his feet up onto the bed and died, and he was added to his people.
verses.50:1: Seeing this, Joseph fell down on his father's face, weeping and kissing him.
verses.50:2: And he commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father with spices.
verses.50:3: While they were fulfilling the orders, forty days passed, for indeed this was the custom for embalmed corpses; and Egypt wept for him seventy days.
verses.50:4: And when the time of mourning was completed, Joseph spoke to the household of Pharaoh, saying, "If I have found favor in your sight, speak in the ears of Pharaoh,
verses.50:5: because my father put me under oath, saying, 'Look, I am dying; in my tomb, which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, you will bury me.' Therefore I will go up, and bury my father, and return."
verses.50:6: And Pharaoh said to him, "Go up and bury your father, just as you were put under oath."
verses.50:7: As he went up, there went with him all the elders of the house of Pharaoh and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
verses.50:8: and the house of Joseph with his brothers, except for the little ones, and the flocks and herds, which they had left behind in the land of Goshen.
verses.50:9: He also had chariots and horsemen in his retinue, and it became no small crowd.
verses.50:10: And they came to the Threshing Floor of Atad, which is situated across the Jordan, where they completed seven days, observing the funeral rites with great and intense mourning.
verses.50:11: When the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw this, they said, "This is a great mourning for the Egyptians." And for that reason the name of that place was called Mourning of Egypt.
verses.50:12: Therefore the sons of Jacob did just as he had commanded them;
verses.50:13: and carrying him into the land of Canaan, they buried him in the double cave, which Abraham had bought with the field as a possession for a tomb from Ephron the Hittite, facing Mamre.
verses.50:14: And Joseph returned to Egypt with his brothers and the entire retinue, after his father had been buried.
verses.50:15: When he was dead, his brothers, being afraid and saying to one another, "Perhaps he remembers the wrong that he suffered and may repay us all the evil that we did,"
verses.50:16: sent word to him, saying, "Your father commanded us before he died,
verses.50:17: that we should say these things to you in his words: 'I implore you to forget the crime of your brothers, and the sin and malice that they practiced against you.' We also plead that you forgive the servants of the God of your father this iniquity." Upon hearing these things, Joseph wept.
verses.50:18: And his brothers came to him and, prostrate on the ground, bowed down and said, "We are your servants."
verses.50:19: He answered them, "Do not be afraid. Can we resist the will of God?
verses.50:20: You planned evil against me, yet God turned it to good, so that He might exalt me, as you see at present, and save many peoples.
verses.50:21: Do not be afraid; I will nourish you and your little ones." And he consoled them and spoke kindly and gently.
verses.50:22: And he dwelt in Egypt with all his father's house, and lived one hundred and ten years. And he saw Ephraim's children to the third generation. The children of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were also born on Joseph's knees.
verses.50:23: After these things had passed, he spoke to his brothers, "After my death God will visit you and cause you to go up from this land to the land that He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."
verses.50:24: And when he had put them under oath and said, "God will visit you; carry my bones away with you from this place,"
verses.50:25: he died, when one hundred and ten years of his life were completed. And embalmed with spices, he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

notes.1:1: Latin cælum is singular ("heaven"), unlike Hebrew plural hashshamayim ("the heavens").
notes.1:2: Latin inanis et vacua literally means "empty and vacant"; ferebatur ("was borne" or "moved") renders the Spirit's motion over the waters.
notes.1:6: Latin firmamentum denotes a solid vault or expanse; rendered "expanse" to maintain modern vocabulary.
notes.1:29: Latin ecce ("look") introduces the grant of plant food; rendered "Look" rather than archaic "behold."
notes.2:1: Latin cæli is plural here ("the heavens"), contrasting with singular cælum in 1:1; ornatus literally means "adornment" or "array."
notes.2:6: Latin fons means "spring" or "fountain" rather than "mist."
notes.2:7: Latin de limo terræ means "from the clay/mud of the earth," and in faciem ejus means "into his face" (rather than "nostrils").
notes.2:8: Latin paradisum voluptatis a principio literally reads "a paradise of delight from the beginning" (rendering Hebrew Eden as "delight" and miqqedem temporally as "from the beginning").
notes.2:11: Latin spellings Phison and Hevilath are rendered with standard modern English Pishon and Havilah.
notes.2:13: Latin spelling Gehon is rendered Gihon; Æthiopiæ is translated directly from the Latin as "Ethiopia."
notes.2:17: Latin morte morieris ("by death you will die") is an emphatic Hebraic idiom rendered "you will surely die."
notes.2:18: Latin faciamus ("let Us make") is first-person plural, agreeing with the Septuagint against Hebrew singular "I will make."
notes.2:23: Latin preserves the Hebrew wordplay with Virago ("woman/heroic woman") derived from vir ("man"); rendered "Woman ... man" in natural modern English.
notes.2:24: Latin erunt duo ("the two will be") explicitly includes "two," agreeing with the Septuagint against the Masoretic Hebrew.
notes.3:4: Latin Nequaquam morte moriemini literally negates the emphatic idiom "die by death" ("By no means will you surely die").
notes.3:6: Latin reads aspectuque delectabile ("delightful in appearance") rather than "desirable to make one wise."
notes.3:8: Latin ligni is grammatically singular ("tree") used collectively for the trees/woods of paradise.
notes.3:12: Latin explicitly adds sociam ("as a companion").
notes.3:14: Latin super pectus tuum literally reads "upon your chest" rather than "on your belly."
notes.3:15: The Vulgate famously reads feminine ipsa conteret ("she will crush") rather than masculine "he/it," and insidiaberis ("you will lie in wait for") for the serpent's action against her heel.
notes.3:16: The Vulgate reads sub viri potestate eris ("you will be under your husband's authority") where the Hebrew reads "your desire shall be for your husband."
notes.3:17: Latin in opere tuo reads "in your work" rather than "because of you."
notes.3:20: Latin spelling Heva is rendered with standard modern English "Eve."
notes.4:7: The Vulgate renders this difficult verse distinctively: "recipies" ("will you not receive"), "statim ... aderit" ("will immediately be present" rather than "crouches"), and "sub te" ("under you" rather than "toward you").
notes.4:8: The Vulgate includes Cain's words "Egrediamur foras" ("Let us go outside"), a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text (and reading "into the field" in the Septuagint).
notes.4:13: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew clause as "quam ut veniam merear" ("too great for me to deserve pardon"), focusing on Cain's inability to merit forgiveness rather than his inability to bear his punishment.
notes.4:16: Rather than treating Hebrew "Nod" as a place name ("the land of Nod"), the Vulgate translates it as "profugus" ("as a fugitive"), directly echoing the curse in 4:12 and 4:14.
notes.4:26: The Vulgate reads the singular subject "iste coepit" ("this one began"), attributing the beginning of calling on the Lord's name specifically to Enosh rather than impersonally to people in general.
notes.5:2: The Vulgate retains "Adam" as a proper name for the pair ("called their name Adam") rather than translating it as a common noun ("Man" or "Humankind").
notes.5:3: Like the Hebrew, the Latin omits an explicit direct object after "genuit" ("fathered"), translated literally here as "fathered one."
notes.5:24: The Vulgate reads "non apparuit" ("he was not seen" or "he did not appear"), corresponding to the Hebrew "he was not" and the Septuagint "he was not found."
notes.5:31: In this text's verse numbering, Genesis 5 ends at verse 31, which includes the notice of Noah's age and his three sons that the Hebrew places in a separate verse 32.
notes.6:3: Vulgate reads "God" (Deus) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the divine name, and renders the debated Hebrew verb yadon as permanebit ("will remain"), agreeing with the Septuagint.
notes.6:4: Vulgate translates Hebrew nephilim as gigantes ("giants"), following the Septuagint, and links the clause with postquam enim ("for after") rather than "and also afterward."
notes.6:6: Clem1598-USFX prints 'hominum' (matching the 1590 Sixtine edition) where accusative singular 'hominem' ('man', Codex Amiatinus) is required by the sense.
notes.6:11: Vulgate renders Hebrew chamas ("violence") here and in 6:13 as iniquitate ("iniquity").
notes.6:14: Vulgate translates the rare Hebrew phrase for gopher wood (atsei gofer) as de lignis laevigatis ("of planed wood" or "smoothed timber").
notes.6:16: Vulgate renders Hebrew tzohar as fenestram ("window"), and specifies the three levels of the ark as deorsum, coenacula et tristega ("lower rooms, second-story chambers, and third stories").
notes.7:4: Latin omnem substantiam ("every substance") renders Hebrew kol ha-yekum ("every existing thing"), as also in 7:23.
notes.7:9: Vulgate reads "the Lord" (Dominus) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "God" (Elohim), as also in 6:22.
notes.7:22: Vulgate reads in terra ("on the earth") and omits "in its nostrils" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies "in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, of all that was on dry land."
notes.8:4: Vulgate reads "the twenty-seventh day" (vigesimo septimo die, agreeing with the Septuagint against the Hebrew "seventeenth") and translates Hebrew Ararat as Armeniae ("Armenia").
notes.8:7: Vulgate agrees with the Septuagint in reading et non revertebatur ("and did not return"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "going and returning" without a negative.
notes.8:11: Vulgate describes what the dove carried as ramum olivae virentibus foliis ("an olive branch with green leaves"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of a freshly plucked olive leaf.
notes.8:17: Vulgate reads ingredimini super terram ("enter upon the earth"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "let them swarm on the earth."
notes.9:4: The Vulgate omits the Hebrew reference to the flesh's 'life' (or 'soul'), stating simply that flesh with blood must not be eaten.
notes.9:6: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Vulgate omits 'by man' before 'his blood will be shed' and renders the final clause passively ('man was made in the image of God').
notes.9:7: Latin 'ingredimini super terram' ('go forth upon the earth') differs from the Hebrew, which reads 'swarm (or teem) upon the earth.'
notes.9:15: Latin 'quae carnem vegetat' ('that animates flesh') is a distinctive Vulgate rendering for the Hebrew phrase 'of all flesh.'
notes.9:22: In verses 22-23, the Vulgate renders the single Hebrew word for 'nakedness' with three explicit Latin modesty terms ('verenda,' 'verecunda,' and 'virilia').
notes.10:9: Where the Hebrew says 'therefore it is said,' the Vulgate explicitly calls the saying a proverb ('Ob hoc exivit proverbium').
notes.10:11: The Vulgate makes Asshur the subject who went out from Shinar (rather than Nimrod going into Assyria) and translates the Hebrew city name Rehoboth-Ir as a common noun phrase, 'the streets of the city' ('plateas civitatis').
notes.10:15: Where the Hebrew has the personal name Heth, the Vulgate uses the gentilic 'Hethaeum' ('the Hittite'), matching the tribal names that follow.
notes.10:21: The Vulgate's ablative phrasing ('fratre Japheth majore') resolves the ambiguity of the Hebrew syntax by identifying Shem, rather than Japheth, as the older brother.
notes.10:28: The Vulgate reads 'Ebal' (matching 1 Chronicles 1:22 and the Samaritan Pentateuch) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text of Genesis reads 'Obal.'
notes.11:4: Latin celebremus nomen nostrum ("let us make our name renowned") differs in wording from the Hebrew "let us make a name for ourselves."
notes.11:5: Latin filii Adam ("the sons of Adam") renders the Hebrew bene ha-adam ("sons of man") with the name Adam.
notes.11:6: The Vulgate's nec desistent a cogitationibus suis, donec eas opere compleant ("nor will they desist from their plans until they complete them in deed") is a distinctly Latin rendering compared with the Hebrew "nothing that they propose to do will now be impossible for them."
notes.11:13: The Clementine Vulgate reads trecentis tribus annis (303 years) here, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 403 years.
notes.12:2: Latin erisque benedictus ("and you will be blessed") uses a future passive construction, differing from the Hebrew imperative "and be a blessing."
notes.12:5: Latin animas quas fecerant ("the souls whom they had made") literally preserves a Hebrew idiom often understood as either servants acquired or converts won in Haran.
notes.12:6: Latin convallem illustrem ("the illustrious valley") is a distinctly Vulgate rendering of the Hebrew elon Moreh ("the oak/terebinth of Moreh").
notes.12:16: Latin uses the plural verb bene usi sunt ("they treated ... well"), whereas the Hebrew has a singular verb referring specifically to Pharaoh.
notes.13:2: The Vulgate renders Hebrew miqneh ("livestock/possessions") as in possessione ("in the possession of"), yielding "in the possession of gold and silver" without separately listing livestock.
notes.13:11: Latin ab oriente ("from the east") renders the Hebrew miqqedem, which can also mean "eastward."
notes.13:12: Latin habitavit in Sodomis ("lived in Sodom") is distinctly Vulgate; the Hebrew reads "moved his tent as far as Sodom."
notes.13:18: Latin convallem Mambre ("the valley of Mamre") renders the Hebrew elone Mamre ("the oaks/terebinths of Mamre"), as in 12:6.
notes.14:1: The Vulgate identifies Arioch's realm as Pontus (Latin Ponti) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Ellasar, and renders Hebrew Goiim descriptively as "the nations" (Latin gentium).
notes.14:3: The Vulgate translates Hebrew Siddim as "the Woodland Valley" (Latin vallem Silvestrem), understanding the name from a related term for fields or wooded country; the same rendering recurs in verses 8 and 10.
notes.14:5: The Vulgate reads "with them" (Latin cum eis, matching the Septuagint) where the Masoretic Text vocalizes the Hebrew consonants as a place name, "in Ham."
notes.14:6: The Vulgate renders Hebrew El-paran ("terebinth of Paran") as "the Plains of Paran" (Latin Campestria Pharan); similarly, in verse 13 it translates Hebrew "oaks/terebinths of Mamre" as "the valley of Mamre" (Latin convalle Mambre).
notes.14:20: The Vulgate renders this clause "under whose protection the enemies are in your hands" (Latin quo protegente, hostes in manibus tuis sunt), whereas the Hebrew states "who has delivered your enemies into your hand."
notes.15:1: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew metaphor "shield" as "protector" (Latin protector), echoing "under whose protection" in 14:20.
notes.15:2: The Vulgate resolves a difficult Hebrew phrase as "the son of the steward of my house is this Damascus Eliezer" (Latin filius procuratoris domus meae iste Damascus Eliezer).
notes.15:4: Latin de utero tuo literally means "from your belly" or "from your womb," used here in its broader anatomical sense for Abram's own body as the source of his natural heir.
notes.15:6: Following the passive construction also found in the Septuagint and Romans 4:3, the Latin reads passive "it was credited to him" (reputatum est illi) rather than the Hebrew active "He reckoned it to him."
notes.16:2: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom "be built up from her" as "obtain children from her" (Latin ex illa suscipiam filios).
notes.16:7: The Clementine Vulgate combines both 'on the way to Shur' and 'in the desert' (in via Sur in deserto).
notes.16:12: The Vulgate simplifies Hebrew "a wild donkey of a man" to "a wild man" (Latin ferus homo), and renders Hebrew "he will dwell" concretely as "he will pitch tents" (Latin figet tabernacula).
notes.16:13: Where the Hebrew phrasing is notoriously elliptical and often taken as a question, the Vulgate gives a declarative exclamation echoing Exodus 33:23: "Truly here I have seen the back of Him who sees me" (Latin Profecto hic vidi posteriora videntis me).
notes.17:4: Latin "Ego sum" ("I am") renders the emphatic Hebrew pronoun phrase ("As for Me, look").
notes.17:6: Latin "in gentibus" (ablative, "among the nations") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("into nations").
notes.17:16: The Vulgate uses masculine pronouns ("cui ... eritque ... ex eo"), applying the second blessing and the descent of nations and kings to the promised son rather than to Sarah as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:24: The Vulgate uses the active verb "circumcidit" ("when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses the passive ("when he was circumcised").
notes.18:1: The Vulgate reads "in convalle Mambre" ("in the valley of Mamre"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to the oaks or terebinths of Mamre.
notes.18:10: Latin "vita comite" (literally "with life as companion," repeated in 18:14) is a classical Latin ablative absolute rendering the Hebrew idiom for the return of the season next year, meaning if life continues.
notes.18:19: Latin "propter Abraham" ("for Abraham's sake") differs slightly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("upon Abraham").
notes.18:25: The Vulgate renders the closing clause as a negative statement with "nequaquam" ("You who judge all the earth will by no means execute this judgment"), unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text's rhetorical question ("Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justice?").
notes.18:28: The Sixto-Clementine Vulgate distinctively reads 'propter quadraginta quinque' ('because of forty-five') where the Hebrew text and Codex Amiatinus read 'because of five.'
notes.19:17: In v. 18 Lot speaks to "them" ("ad eos") while addressing a single spokesperson as lowercase "domine mi" ("my lord").
notes.19:22: The Latin spells Zoar as "Segor" (following the Septuagint transliteration of Hebrew Tsoar, linked to "small" in v. 20).
notes.19:26: The Vulgate reads "statuam salis" ("a statue of salt"), rather than the Hebrew "pillar of salt."
notes.19:29: The Vulgate reads "civitates regionis illius" ("the cities of that region") where the Hebrew has "the cities of the valley."
notes.19:38: Whereas the Hebrew gives the son's name as Ben-ammi ("son of my people"), the Vulgate writes "Ammon" directly and supplies the explanatory gloss "id est, Filius populi mei" ("that is, 'Son of my people'").
notes.20:4: The Vulgate follows the Septuagint in reading "gentem ignorantem et justam" ("an unknowing and righteous nation"), whereas the Hebrew reads "even a righteous nation."
notes.20:8: The Vulgate specifies "Statimque de nocte" ("And immediately in the night"), whereas the Hebrew reads "early in the morning."
notes.20:16: Distinctively in the Vulgate, Abimelech's closing words read "et quocumque perrexeris: mementoque te deprehensam" ("and wherever you go; and remember that you were caught"), whereas the Hebrew reads "and before all you are vindicated."
notes.21:2: Latin in senectute sua ("in her old age") refers reflexively to Sarah, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "to Abraham in his old age."
notes.21:7: The Clementine Vulgate reads nominative 'Quis auditurus crederet Abraham' (literally 'Who, about to hear / upon hearing, would believe Abraham...'; Codex Amiatinus reads accusative 'auditurum', 'that Abraham would hear'), whereas the Hebrew reads 'Who would have said to Abraham... children.'
notes.21:9: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate explicitly adds cum Isaac filio suo ("playing with Isaac, her son"), expanding the shorter Hebrew participle meaning "laughing" or "mocking."
notes.21:32: Here the Vulgate translates Beersheba as pro puteo juramenti ("for the well of the oath") and moves Abimelech and Phicol's departure to the start of verse 33; verse 33 also renders the Hebrew tamarisk tree as nemus ("a grove"), and verse 34 uses Palæstinorum as a Latin variant for the Philistines (cf. Philistinorum in verse 33).
notes.22:2: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "land of Moriah" interpretively as terram visionis ("the land of vision"), connecting it to "The Lord sees" in verse 14; it also uses unigenitum ("only-begotten," repeated in verses 12 and 16).
notes.22:6: Here and in verse 10 the Vulgate translates the Hebrew slaughter-knife as gladium ("sword"); in verses 7 and 8 it similarly renders Hebrew "lamb" as victima ("victim").
notes.22:13: Latin post tergum ("behind his back") reflects reading the Hebrew text as "behind" rather than "one/a," and vepres renders the thicket specifically as "briers."
notes.22:14: Latin Dominus videt ("The Lord sees") and In monte Dominus videbit ("On the mountain the Lord will see") render the place-name and proverb literally with "see," echoing "the land of vision" in verse 2.
notes.22:21: Latin patrem Syrorum ("the father of the Syrians") renders the Hebrew name Aram with the classical ethnic designation "Syrians," following the Septuagint.
notes.23:1: The Clementine Vulgate ends after Sarah's age, omitting the Hebrew closing clause ('these were the years of the life of Sarah').
notes.23:3: Latin 'ab officio funeris' literally means 'from the duty/rites of the funeral,' an idiomatic Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew has 'from before his dead.'
notes.23:9: Latin 'speluncam duplicem' ('the double cave'; also in vv. 17, 19) renders the Hebrew place name Machpelah etymologically as an adjective rather than transliterating it.
notes.23:10: Latin 'Habitabat' ('was living') takes the underlying verb in its sense of dwelling rather than sitting among the sons of Heth at the gate.
notes.23:16: The Vulgate uses the Roman commercial phrase 'probatæ monetæ publicæ' ('of approved public currency'), where the Hebrew reads 'current with the merchant.'
notes.24:22: The Vulgate explicitly reads plural golden earrings weighing two shekels ("inaures aureas, appendentes siclos duos"; cf. v. 30), whereas the Hebrew describes a single gold ring weighing half a shekel.
notes.24:27: The Vulgate specifies that the Lord led the servant "by a straight path" ("recto itinere") into the house of his master's singular "brother" ("fratris"), where the Hebrew reads "in the way" and plural "brothers."
notes.24:47: The Vulgate renders this clause as "I hung the earrings to adorn her face" ("Suspendi itaque inaures ad ornandam faciem ejus"), reconciling plural "earrings" with the Hebrew wording "I put the ring on her nose."
notes.24:53: Here and in v. 55 the Vulgate reads plural "brothers" ("fratribus" / "fratres"), whereas the Hebrew reads singular "her brother."
notes.24:62: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place names Beer-lahai-roi ("the well whose name is Of the Living and Seeing One," "Viventis et videntis") and the Negev ("the southern land," "in terra australi") rather than transliterating them.
notes.25:9: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Machpelah literally as "spelunca duplici" ("the double cave").
notes.25:11: Instead of transliterating the Hebrew Beer-lahai-roi, the Vulgate translates it as "puteum nomine Viventis et videntis" ("the well by the name of the Living and Seeing One").
notes.25:15: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'Hadar' (with some Hebrew manuscripts) where other traditions read 'Hadad.'
notes.25:18: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew verb "naphal" (often understood as "settled") as "obiit" ("he died"), giving "he died in the presence of all his brothers."
notes.25:22: The Vulgate renders the elliptical Hebrew question ("If so, why am I like this?") explicitly as "Si sic mihi futurum erat, quid necesse fuit concipere?" ("If it was going to be this way for me, what need was there to conceive?").
notes.25:27: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "ish sadeh" ("man of the field") as "homo agricola" ("a farmer") and "ish tam" ("a quiet/complete man") as "vir simplex" ("a simple man").
notes.26:1: The Vulgate refers to the Philistines as "Palæstini" (genitive "Palæstinorum") in vv. 1, 8, and 14, and as "Philisthiim" in v. 18.
notes.26:20: In vv. 20-22 the Vulgate translates the Hebrew well names Esek, Sitnah, and Rehoboth into Latin as "Calumniam" ("False Claim"), "Inimicitias" ("Hostility"), and "Latitudo" ("Spaciousness").
notes.26:29: Instead of a separate final exclamation ("You are now the blessed of the Lord"), the Vulgate closes the sentence with a participial phrase: "auctum benedictione Domini" ("enriched by the blessing of the Lord").
notes.26:33: The Vulgate translates the well's name as "Abundantiam" ("Abundance"), reading the Hebrew consonants as "sava" (plenty/satiety) rather than "Shibah" (oath/seven).
notes.27:20: Vulgate reads 'It was the will of God that what I wanted should quickly come before me' (Voluntas Dei fuit...), without specifying 'the Lord your God' as in the Hebrew text.
notes.27:29: Vulgate renders the final clause as 'let him be filled with blessings' (benedictionibus repleatur), expanding on the simpler Hebrew 'be blessed.'
notes.27:39: Vulgate adds 'being moved' (motus) and reads positively 'In the richness... and in the dew... your blessing will be' (benedictio tua in v. 40), whereas the Hebrew has 'your dwelling' and is often construed privatively ('away from').
notes.28:2: Vulgate renders Hebrew Paddan-aram as 'Mesopotamia of Syria' (here and in vv. 5-6), and correspondingly uses 'the Syrian' and 'Syria' in vv. 5 and 7.
notes.28:4: Vulgate reads plural 'blessings' and 'which He promised to your grandfather' (quam pollicitus est avo tuo), where the Hebrew has singular 'blessing' and 'which God gave to Abraham.'
notes.28:13: Vulgate renders 'leaning upon the ladder' (innixum scalae), giving a concrete sense to the Hebrew phrase that can mean 'standing above it' or 'standing beside him.'
notes.29:1: The Vulgate condenses the Hebrew idiom ('lifted up his feet and went to the land of the sons of the east') into 'set out and came to the eastern land' (terram orientalem).
notes.29:12: The Vulgate literally translates the broad Hebrew term for kinsman as 'brother' (frater patris sui), though v. 13 identifies Jacob more specifically as Laban's sister's son.
notes.29:17: Vulgate 'lippis erat oculis' ('had bleary eyes') gives a distinctly physical rendering of Hebrew rakkot ('soft' or 'weak').
notes.29:22: Where the Hebrew has 'gathered all the men of the place and made a feast,' the Vulgate reads 'having called many crowds of friends to a banquet, he held the wedding.'
notes.29:35: Vulgate 'confitebor Domino' (lit. 'I will confess/acknowledge the Lord') is the standard biblical Latin expression for offering praise and thanksgiving to God, reflecting the wordplay behind the name Judah.
notes.30:8: Vulgate "Comparavit me Deus cum sorore mea" ("God has matched/compared me with my sister") reflects Jerome's rendering of the Naphtali wordplay as a competitive comparison, whereas the Hebrew reads "with mighty wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister."
notes.30:27: Vulgate "experimento didici" ("I have learned by experience") renders a Hebrew verb meaning "learned by divination" in terms of practical observation. Here the Vulgate also reads "Deus" ("God") where the Hebrew has the divine name (compare 30:6 and 30:22, where the Vulgate reads "Dominus" for Hebrew Elohim).
notes.30:35: The Vulgate distinctively reports that Laban delivered the entire single-colored flock ("of white and black fleece") into his sons' hands (matching 30:40, where all white and black animals belong to Laban and Jacob sets rods before the rams), whereas the Hebrew has Laban entrusting the striped, speckled, spotted, and dark animals to his sons.
notes.30:41: In verses 41-42 the Vulgate renders the contrast seasonally as "primo tempore" ("at the first season") versus "serotina admissura ... et conceptus extremus" ("late mating and final conception"), reflecting an ancient interpretive tradition that identified early-season lambs with stronger stock and late-season lambs with weaker stock.
notes.31:8: In the Vulgate, Laban's second condition specifies alba ("white"), whereas the Hebrew has "striped" (or "streaked").
notes.31:24: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom "from good to bad" here as aspere ("harshly"), and similarly as durius ("too harsh") in 31:29.
notes.31:42: The Vulgate reads nudum ("naked"), whereas the Hebrew has "empty-handed."
notes.31:47: Rather than transliterating the Aramaic and Hebrew place names (Jegar-sahadutha and Galeed), the Vulgate translates both directly into Latin (Tumulus testis and Acervum testimonii) and adds "each according to the idiom of his own language."
notes.32:2: The explanatory gloss "that is, Camp" (id est, Castra) is added in the Vulgate and does not appear in the Hebrew text; Latin castra is grammatically plural, echoing the dual Hebrew name Mahanaim ("Two Camps").
notes.32:25: The Vulgate reads emarcuit ("withered") here and in 32:33 (adding et obstipuerit, "and it grew numb"), whereas the Hebrew indicates that Jacob's hip socket was dislocated.
notes.32:28: Distinctively, the Vulgate expresses the explanation of the name Israel as an a fortiori question ("if you have been strong against God, how much more will you prevail against men?"), whereas the Hebrew has a declarative statement ("you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed").
notes.33:4: The Vulgate uses the singular verb flevit ("he wept"), referring specifically to Esau, whereas the Hebrew has the plural ("they wept").
notes.33:11: The Vulgate links the final clause back to "the blessing" through a participle describing God ("and that God has granted to me, bestowing all things"), whereas the Hebrew has Jacob state that God has dealt graciously with him and that he has everything.
notes.33:18: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate treats Salem as a proper place name ("Salem, the city of the Shechemites"), where the Hebrew word can also be read as the adverb "safely," and renders Hebrew Paddan-aram as "Mesopotamia of Syria."
notes.33:19: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate renders the rare Hebrew unit qesitah as "lambs" (centum agnis).
notes.33:20: Rather than having Jacob name the altar "El-Elohe-Israel" as in the Hebrew, the Vulgate has him call upon "the most mighty God of Israel" over the altar.
notes.34:2: The Vulgate adds 'fell in love with her' (adamavit) and renders the final clause as 'overpowering the virgin by force' (vi opprimens virginem), where the Hebrew simply has 'took her, lay with her, and humbled her.'
notes.34:21: The Vulgate interprets the Hebrew idiom 'wide of hands' as 'being spacious and wide it needs cultivators' (quae spatiosa et lata cultoribus indiget), expanding on the theme of open land.
notes.34:22: Latin 'Unum est quo differtur tantum bonum' ('There is one thing by which so great a good is delayed') is a distinctive Vulgate rendering of the Hebrew condition ('Only on this condition will the men consent to live with us').
notes.34:25: Latin 'confidenter' ('boldly') applies the Hebrew adverb (often understood as 'unsuspectingly' of the city) to Simeon and Levi's confident entry; the Vulgate also specifies 'when the pain of the wounds is most severe' (quando gravissimus vulnerum dolor est).
notes.35:7: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name El-bethel as 'House of God' (Domus Dei), and likewise translates Allon-bacuth in v. 8 as 'Oak of Weeping' (Quercus fletus) and Paddan-aram in vv. 9 and 26 as 'Mesopotamia of Syria' (Mesopotamiam Syriae).
